LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.

According to recent reports, but as early voting surged in mid-October, she sensed she might pull off an upset over Republican Rep. Tim Moore, the influential former speaker of the North Carolina House and a chief architect of the gerrymander that aimed to keep the 14th District safely red.

“There were a lot of pins and needles,” noted Womack, a 49-year-old ordained minister who works at a Charlotte-based nonprofit. After seeing long lines at polling places extend into Election Day, she grew more confident: “People were ready to exercise their voice.”.

Womack – who raised less than $60,000 to Moore’s $2.1 million – eked out a 2-point win in the district, which reaches from the Charlotte suburbs to mountain counties in the west.

Sources indicate that saddled with an unpopular president and broad dissatisfaction with the status quo, Republican incumbents across the nation experienced a midterm drubbing last week. As of Monday evening, House Democrats had netted 42 seats, with more races left to be called. The GOP in North Carolina, a state that Trump carried three times, was among the hardest hit.

In a recent development, democrats have so far flipped five House seats in the Tar Heel State. Besides Womack, the “blue tsunami” also swept in Paul Barringer, a lawyer who founded an outdoor clothing line, and High Point Mayor Cyril Jefferson. And Army veteran Richard Ojeda, who once served in the West Virginia Senate, defeated Rep. Richard Hudson, the chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee.

Democrats also won two races that had been seen as competitive for much of the cycle. Farmer Jamie Ager flipped an open seat in the state’s mountain west, while Rep. Don Davis held on to his Eastern North Carolina district, which Republicans had redrawn in their favor.

Meanwhile, in the state’s hilly northwest corner, 11-term Republican Virginia Foxx, the chairwoman of the powerful Rules Committee, is fighting for her political future: As of Monday afternoon, former journalist Chuck Hubbard led her by 99 votes in the 5th District, though The Associated Press had yet to call the race.

Sources indicate that that was also true in the neighboring 10th District, where GOP incumbent Pat Harrigan had a 1-point edge over Democratic physician associate Ashley Bell. Also uncalled were a pair of contests in Eastern North Carolina, where Republican Rep. Greg Murphy clung to a 233-vote edge over Democratic former state Rep. Raymond Smith and GOP Rep. David Rouzer led Democratic social worker Kimberly Hardy by less than a point.

“Nobody could have predicted this,’’ mentioned David Wilson Brown, who leads the Democratic Party in Gaston County near Charlotte and has lost two bids for the House, including to Foxx in 2020. “It’s a watershed moment.”.

The Democratic rout in the midterm elections was powered by victories in states with new GOP-favored maps, including Texas, Ohio and Florida.

Recent findings suggest that but Democrats’ success in North Carolina was especially striking given the steep structural disadvantages the party faced. Since Republicans flipped the state legislature in 2010, and with it control of the redistricting process, no House GOP incumbent had lost a general election in the Tar Heel State until last week.

This year’s  congressional map – the state's sixth in seven election cycles – was engineered by the Republican-led legislature to help the party capture 11 of the state's 14 House seats.

But the Democratic surge was so significant that it easily overpowered the GOP’s built-in edge. Democratic candidates were also lifted by former Gov. Roy Cooper, whose 20-point Senate win provided the underticket with powerful coattails.

Industry observers note that “In order for them to gerrymander our state in the way that they did, they were spread very thin,” Brown said, referring to state Republicans. “So they were kind of ripe to be defeated that way.”.

In a recent development, the repeated rounds of redistricting may have also erased some of the advantages of incumbency, according to Peter L. Francia, a political science professor at East Carolina University. “If you carve up a district every two years, you've taken away some of that [advantage]. And I think that that came back and hurt Republicans in this cycle.”.

Doug Heye, a GOP strategist and a former spokesman for the Republican National Committee, said redistricting “ticked off a whole lot of voters, and really activated the Democratic base.”.

On the Republican side, voters were “less motivated because they were unexcited about Trump,’’ Heye added.

Republican incumbents accustomed to winning by comfortable margins weren’t prepared for a political environment driven by anger over the war in Iran and angst about the rising cost of living.

“Clearly, a lot of those Republicans didn’t take their elections seriously,” Heye remarked. “They won last time with 18 points. They weren't on anyone's radar screen, so they didn't think they had to do anything.”.

In a recent development, womack credits her win to a grassroots campaign centered on economic concerns. While her race wasn’t on the national radar – Moore, after all, won by 16 points in 2024 – and her campaign didn’t have money for ads, she was out in the district doing events every day.

“There are a lot of working families right now who are in the missing middle,” she stated in an interview. “They make too much money to get help, but they don't make enough money to get ahead. … Someone who can be working a full-time job, but still doesn’t have enough money to buy groceries or to afford their medications or to have access to health insurance.”.

In a recent development, womack noted her own struggles have shaped her approach to politics. This week, she’s slated to appear in court on a felony charge for allegedly failing to return a rental car in 2019. The incident wound up in one of Moore’s attack ads.

It has been revealed that “There are so many people who [understand] what happens when you're down on your luck and you don't have enough money to make good financial decisions,’’ she said. “Most people don't want those bad decisions to be a definition of their character for the rest of their life.”.

Early in the midterm cycle, Democratic opposition research group American Bridge prepared detailed dossiers on Republican House incumbents in North Carolina.

Recent findings suggest that “Someone like Virginia Foxx, she’s been on the Hill forever,” said Pat Dennis, the group’s president. “She was somebody … who under the radar could be vulnerable. So we started really early.”.

It has been revealed that american Bridge’s political arm spent $340,000 on ads targeting Foxx. One spot featured a man who identified himself as a Trump voter expressing anger at the government’s response to Hurricane Helene, which devastated the mountain communities of Western North Carolina two years ago.

Other Democrats scoffed at the group’s decision to spend money targeting entrenched Republicans far from the main House battleground.

“There was a lot of reluctance from people to really believe that that data was correct, but it was,’’ Dennis stated. “Then over the summer, we saw her numbers collapsing, so we put paid media behind it and it really paid off.”.

Hubbard ran against Foxx two years ago and lost by almost 20 points.

According to recent reports, “I kind of had a notion I was going to do this again,’’ he said in an interview Saturday while en route to Washington for freshman orientation. “I don’t like to lose at checkers, much less a congressional race.”.

After a court-drawn map resulted in a split North Carolina delegation after the 2022 elections, state Republicans won back control of the map-making process and went on to win 10 of the state’s 14 House seats under a newly introduced map two years later.

At Trump’s urging, Republicans made further tweaks to the North Carolina map last year, but the original gerrymander finally came back to bite the GOP in 2026, according to Hubbard.

According to recent reports, “North Carolina is one of the most severely gerrymandered states,’’ he said. “And what happened was they had to steal from Peter to pay Paul. It's been referred to by political scientists as a dummymander.”.

As the vote count in the 5th District continues, Foxx, whose campaign declined to comment for this story, has requested the presence of nonpartisan election observers.

They “will serve as crucial, watchful eyes to ensure that this sacred process is not impeded and that all legal votes are counted in a consistent, thorough manner,’’ she posted on social media.

But even before the final races are called, Republicans are already looking to the next election.

Heye, who expects North Carolina to remain a purple state in 2028 and beyond, cautioned the Democrats who won last week not to get too comfortable in Washington. He invoked Fred Heineman, the former Raleigh police chief who rode the 1994 “Republican Revolution” to Congress – and lasted a single term.

“Some of them will lose, and some of the people who lost may run two years from now and get their seat back,’’ he stated.

One GOP operative, who requested anonymity to speak candidly, offered up a similar assessment.

Trump “didn't keep his promises” and that “just got voters very angry and suppressed the GOP base from coming out because, in a midterm election it's a base turnout contest,’’ the strategist remarked.

“But these Democrats are renting these districts for two years.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, for one glorious moment, the world appears to be united. Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived, to near-universal acclaim, with millions of people abandoning work, school, and presumably all their other responsibilities to explore the streets of Vice City. In these divided times, it's enough to warm the cockles of your heart.

And amid all the fast cars, guns, nightclubs, and criminal capers, there's something else we pay attention to here at Esquire HQ: the watches!

Rockstar Games' latest blockbuster reportedly features 34 "collectible" luxury watches scattered throughout its fictional version of Florida. But that's only part of the story. GTA VI also has its own watch brands, although some of the designs look ... suspiciously familiar.

There's Crowex (a dead ringer for Rolex), Takio (distinctly Casio-adjacent), and Covgari, whose watches owe more to Audemars Piguet than the Italian-o jeweller its name suggests.

From gold Day-Dates to pocket-money Casio digitals, here are some of our favorite real-world watches that appear to have inspired the game's timepieces.

Sources indicate that the gold Crowex is a near dead ringer for the Rolex Day-Date 40 (ref. 228238). The fluted bezel, black dial, and day window at 12 o'clock are all present and correct, although the bracelet differs somewhat from Rolex's iconic President. The Day-Date celebrates its 70th anniversary this year. Evidently, it remains the universal symbol of having made it, even in the virtual world.

The silver chronograph worn by a character overlooking Vice City has more than a passing resemblance to the mighty Daytona. The round case, contrasting sub-dials, and metal bracelet suggest that famous racing chronograph. As we know, the Daytona is one of the world's most sought-after sports watches, making it a natural fit for GTA's world of expensive cars, conspicuous consumption, and bling.

Brian Heder, a veteran drug smuggler, wears a metal sports watch that certainly seems to recall Rolex's Sub. There's the substantial case, dark dial, and the bracelet. The Submariner has been a fixture of luxury watchmaking since 1953, and its more ostentatious steel-and-gold versions would be right at home on the streets of Vice City.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

Industry observers note that jason Duval, one of GTA VI's two protagonists, wears a chunky digital watch resembling something from Casio's Pro Trek range. The large circular display, prominent buttons and rugged case certainly suggest its something from the range of the Japanese juggernaut. A more practical choice than the gold watches favored by some of his associates.

In-game equivalent: Takio Digital Watch.

It has been revealed that not everyone in Vice City is wearing a gold Rollie lookalike. The Takio F-BLAST is an unmistakable nod to Casio's inexpensive digital classics, particularly the bestselling F-91W. It has the familiar rectangular display, black dial surround, and simple, functional design. There's even a more colorful version, with a red case and two-tone metal bracelet, spotted in the game's Hamlet Thrift store.

As spotted by watch Instagram account @geesgshock.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando just got married in Frank Sinatra’s Palm Springs backyard. The singer and the Liily drummer, who met on a blind date in 2021, exchanged vows on Saturday, November 21, beneath an arch of white flowers at the edge of Sinatra’s former swimming pool. As far as wedding backdrops go, this one makes sense for two musicians: The pool is shaped like a grand piano.

Sinatra’s former home takes its name from the two palms that still stand on the property. When he hired architect E. Stewart Williams in 1947, he wanted a Georgian-style house, but Williams talked him into a single-story design with wide stretches of glass shaded by deep eaves. It was his first residential commission in Palm Springs, and he arranged the house around the pool. From the living room, sliding glass doors open onto a terrace bordered by the house, a pergola, and a cabana.

For a house built for Sinatra, a pool shaped like a grand piano sounds almost too on the nose. But Williams noted the resemblance was incidental: He intended the curve to draw the eye toward the mountains. Sinatra lived at Twin Palms for about six years, including part of his marriage to Ava Gardner. In 2011, Palm Springs granted historic status to the house and parts of its grounds.

Yes, though it’s a private residence, not a museum. The estate is available as a vacation rental, with four bedrooms and room for up to eight guests. It also offers private guided tours for groups of 20 or more.

It has been revealed that the theme this week is shearling jackets. Three-of-thirteen gives a pretty clear look at what the best of the week really was leading into fall. First, we have Fortela, which released an absolutely insane reproduction of a grizzly jacket. With shearling on the outside panel, I’ve always wondered why the grizzly shape never stuck around much after the World Wars, but I have been seeing it pop up a lot more as vintage and reproduction recently. Otherwise, I’m into this Husbands bomber as well as this ladies’ shearling bomber from Buck Mason.

Elsewhere, it’s more confirmation that we are hitting the twilight weeks of 2026. It’s all sweater season and travel. In that section, Globe Trotter is the week’s major winner. The brand’s new polycarbonate suitcase gives it a bit more modern traveler appeal, but the look is still unmistakably Globe Trotter. It’s a rare pairing you don’t see too much. If you’re looking for a suitcase to handle all your holiday travel, I can’t think of anything better to recommend; this is the pinnacle. Scroll, shop, and enjoy.

My problem with Fortela is that the reproductions are so good I don’t even want to keep hunting for the real thing. An interwar grizzly jacket is a grail for me. This one, made in partnership with Italian motorcycle clothing brand Shangri-La Heritage, is so good that I’d feel like an idiot paying $2,000 for a vintage one. —Luke Guillory, commerce editor.

Noah and Converse just released their second Chuck 70 collaboration, reimagining Converse’s cult-favorite silhouette in Noah’s signature tartan, this time in navy and green. —Emma Saxon, contributing fashion assistant.

An unfathomably good Christmas cardigan from Thom Browne’s capsule collection that’s exclusive to Mr Porter. Fair Isle motif on the four-bar pairs with the Fair Isle Hector (Thom Browne’s dachshund mascot) on the back. —L.G.

Sources indicate that I’m a huge Globe-Trotter fan, so when I heard about its lightest suitcase ever was made out of polycarbonate (like every brand does these days) I was scared. Upon review, I was wrong; its absolutely smashed it out of the park. Modern amenities with a look all it’s own—reset of the market should take notes. —L.G.

On the other side of the luxury suitcase aisle, Margiela paint on a Rimowa really, really gets me. I’m a sucker for the patina gimmick. —L.G.

Irish design organization Orior is making some of my favorite out of anyone in the world. Design-forward without being too cerebral—just laser focused on material and craft. —L.G.

The best tee on the market, now made from the best cotton in the world. —L.G.

According to recent reports, every year when that first fall chill hits, I try to find a scarf that beats what Begg x Co. makes. This year marks five years of being unsuccessful in that search; this is the scarf you want. —L.G.

It has been revealed that I talk about Casatlantic in this column every season. The fall-winter collection goes to classic charcoal and navy—incredible. —L.G.

What I wouldn’t give. . . —L.G.

Carl Friedrik makes some of my favorite luggage ever. This week, we got a new collection of compact leather crossbody bags, perfect for everything from running errands to going to a nice dinner to going on a fancy vacation. —Bellamy Richardson, associate commerce editor.

Sorry to overdose on shearling jackets, but this one jumped out at me from Buck Mason’s holiday collection. In fact, all of Buck Mason’s women’s jumped out at me. The men’s stuff is good, but women’s is god-tier. Boys, take my lead and buy your lady a gift this season. —L.G.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

It has been revealed that I have to admit, I have a bit of a gripe with washable rugs. For years, the design industry has been trying to convince us that the answer to a beautiful, livable home is a washable rug. And while I understand the appeal, especially as a mom to two young kids, a dog, and a household that sees its fair share of spills, muddy shoes, and general chaos, I’ve just never been entirely sold on the idea.

While washable rug options have definitely improved over the years, there’s still something about the weight, texture, and character of a traditional rug that I find hard to forgo for the sake of washability. I want a rug that feels substantial underfoot, looks better with age, and doesn’t require me to wrestle an eight-by-ten-foot piece of fabric into my washing machine every time someone spills a juice box.

Sources indicate that when I learned about Ernesta’s protective rug treatment, I was intrigued. The custom rug brand offers an optional treatment designed to help repel spills and make everyday messes easier to clean, without requiring you to compromise on your rug’s style, material, or size. In theory, it offers the best of both worlds: the look and feel of a beautifully made rug, with a little extra insurance against the realities of family life. Plus, it’s a treatment that’s typically hard to access on your own without going custom through a designer.

According to recent reports, I actually have several Ernesta rugs in my home (I’m a huge fan of their quality and approachable customization options!), but after swapping in an Ernesta rug treated with the brand’s protective finish in our living room, I don’t think I’ll ever go back to ordering a rug without it. Here’s what you should know about the treatment, how it's held up in my own home, and why I think it may be a smarter investment than yet another washable rug.

Best for: This rug is an excellent option for families, pet owners, or anyone who just prefers not to have to be too precious with their things.

Not ideal for: Anyone looking for a quick-ship rug option.

Bottom Line: The customization of Ernesta’s rug assortment makes it easy to get the exact look and function that serves your home best, including different sizes, non-slip bases, and protections.

One of the reasons I love Ernesta so much is how approachable they make the ordering process. There’s no visiting a showroom or making 400 phone calls to try to get the right custom-cut size. You simply log on to their site, browse the options, then choose up to five samples to try for just $10.

Recent findings suggest that my samples came incredibly quickly—within a few days, they were at my doorstep, ready for review. Because I already liked the look of the rug we had in our living room (more on that later), I knew I didn’t want to stray too far from the neutral, functional foundation it gave us.

When we started, we had Ernesta’s Emerson sisal rug in the space. The nubby texture and color looked beautiful, but it was a bit small (it was originally sized to an old home that we have since moved from), and the deeper grooves of the weave made it hard to clean up spills. I have two young kids and a dog, and truly not a day goes by where someone hasn’t spilled yogurt or cracker crumbs or juice on the rug.

Still, I don’t think you should have to sacrifice beauty for function in a family home, and Ernesta helped us find that balance. After debating between a few different styles, I ended up settling on the Cally wool flatweave rug in Camel. Wool flatweave rugs are notoriously durable on their own, and I knew the protective coating would only help it hold up better. Bonus: The tighter weave meant fewer nooks and crannies for gunk to get into.

Once we decided on our new style, we measured out the size we’d need, which ended up being around 13 x 15 feet. I loved how easy it was to order the exact size we needed for our space, especially given that it wasn’t a standard measurement. If you’re unsure about the right size for your rug (or how many legs of your furniture should be on the rug at one time), Ernesta has helpful guidance on their site.

Placing the order was easy; you can opt into the protective treatment before adding the order to your cart, as well as choose other details, like the type of edge binding and whether you’d like to include a rug pad (we chose the attached version).

Protective treatments for rugs are nothing latest; they’ve been available to design industry insiders for years. That said, very few DTC companies offer the treatment, unless you’re buying through a designer or want to seek out a supplier on your own.

According to recent reports, that’s what’s so great about Ernesta’s offerings—it’s literally as easy as checking a box before you add your rug to cart. The treatment starts at $62 and increases depending on the size of your rug. Their formula is non-toxic and works by acting as a protective layer between the surface of the rug and any spills or debris, preventing stains from setting in and keeping the fibers intact for longer.

Sources indicate that receiving and installing our Ernesta rug couldn’t have been easier, especially considering its large size. It was delivered and placed in our entryway, where it waited for a few days until my husband and I had a spare moment to lay it out.

The rug was packaged beautifully, with thick plastic wrapping protecting the roll, a firm cardboard tube at the center, and fabric wrapping the edges so the binding didn’t get roughed up in transit. I thought this was a particularly nice touch.

As with most rugs, the corners were a bit flared when we first unrolled it, so here’s my favorite tip: add several ice cubes to any corner you want to lay flat and let them melt. The slow dissipation of moisture will relax the rug's fibers, and by the time it has melted away completely, you should have a totally flat rug.

According to recent reports, I was immediately impressed by the look and feel of this rug—the wool was so soft and plush, and the rubber mat integrated on the bottom meant it did not budge once we laid it down (though it did make it difficult to reposition when we laid it a little wonky initially, word to the wise). There was no “chemical” smell from the protective treatments, and the fibers still felt just as soft as they did on the sample I received before ordering.

In a recent development, aesthetically, I love the vibe that this rug brings to the space. It’s soft and plush and cozy, and finally in better proportion with the rest of the room—which is great, because I have a pair of armchairs I won at auction waiting in the wings for their moment. Before, they were floating off the rug and looked odd, but now, they’ll be perfect.

In a recent development, logically, the protective treatment was 100 percent the right choice for our family. Not even five minutes after laying it out, my three-year-old squished an applesauce pouch on the rug, and it came up with ease. In the month since having it, we’ve definitely put this rug through the paces of family life, and it still looks as good as the day we opened it. Cleaning it is easy, and Ernesta has a whole page on their site dedicated to care instructions, depending on the material your rug is made of.

Overall, this is the ideal solution to me: a rug that looks as good as it performs, and doesn’t require any design sacrifice (or yelling from mom) in the process.

What Is a Thanksgiving Cactus? Your Guide to the Other Holiday Cactus

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that by the time the garden has mostly called it a year, the Thanksgiving cactus is just getting started.
  • In a recent development, you’ve probably seen one without knowing exactly what it was.
  • Industry observers note that the Thanksgiving cactus (Schlumbergera truncata) is a flowering cactus native to the forests of Brazil, where it grows on trees instead of in soil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that by the time the garden has mostly called it a year, the Thanksgiving cactus is just getting started. Its red, lavender, or soft salmon flowers appear at the tips of flat green stems, often right around the holiday, and its stems arch over the rim of the pot.

In a recent development, you’ve probably seen one without knowing exactly what it was. Thanksgiving and Christmas cacti often share a shelf and a label (“holiday cactus”), and both can flower in December. The giveaway is in the stems: the Thanksgiving cactus has little pointed teeth along the edges. And it’s far from the kind of cactus you’d put on your sunniest windowsill. It comes from the forests of Brazil, where it grows on trees in filtered light. Here’s what to know about the Thanksgiving cactus.

Industry observers note that the Thanksgiving cactus (Schlumbergera truncata) is a flowering cactus native to the forests of Brazil, where it grows on trees instead of in soil. The flowers, which come in shades including white, red, lavender, and salmon-orange, typically open from mid-November through late December.

It has been revealed that look at one of the flat stem segments. On a Thanksgiving cactus, the edges have pointed teeth; on a true Christmas cactus (Schlumbergera × buckleyi), they’re rounded, like the edge of a scalloped plate.

Set it near an east-facing window or somewhere else with bright, indirect light. When the top inch of potting mix feels dry, water it thoroughly and let the excess drain. If you’ve tucked the nursery pot into a ceramic planter, lift it out to water so it doesn’t end up sitting in a puddle.

Sources indicate that while the plant is budding and flowering, keep the mix lightly moist. You can water less often once the flowers fade. There’s no need to repot it as soon as you bring it home; if it’s outgrown its container, wait until spring and go up one pot size.

According to recent reports, in early fall, give the plant about 14 hours of uninterrupted darkness each night for roughly six weeks. A spare room that gets daylight but where nobody switches on a lamp at night works well. Cool nights—around 55 to 60 degrees Fahrenheit—also encourage buds to form. Once you see buds, keep the plant away from drafts and don’t let the potting mix dry out completely.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that launching this week on Mr Porter is a 17-piece capsule collection created with Newly introduced York’s own Thom Browne. Browne is famed in men’s fashion for his conceptual runway demonstrates—staged in Florence, Milan, Paris and, of course New York—but beneath all the elevated showmanship lies a broad and distinctly wearable aesthetic.

Industry observers note that consisting of casual and tailored pieces and extending to luggage, home goods, and even the recently launched Thom Browne x Bose headphones, the collection puts a youthful twist on Browne’s signature style that blends sportswear and suits with a rigorous attention to detail. Browne has acted as Chairman of the Council of Fashion Designers of America since 1923 and won its prestigious Menswear Designer award four times in his 25-year career.

To showcase the collaboration, the capsule was photographed by Ian Kenneth Bird on young Latest York restaurateur George McNally. If the name McNally rings a bell, that’s no accident; his surname carries a lot of weight in the New York food scene. George is the son of Keith (Balthazar, Minetta Tavern) and nephew of Brian (Indochine), both past masters of creating downtown Manhattan restaurants with an enduring buzz in a notoriously fickle foodie scene.

George—who, at just 23, has worked pretty much every restaurant position going in Upcoming York and London since he was a teenager—is tracing his own culinary path with Faux, his hot new space in Tribeca, serving reasonably priced, loosely French-Mediterranean food, and a space that stays open late for a city that, proverbially, never sleeps.

Go to Mr Porter to see and shop the collection and read George’s accompanying interview.

Above: Inside Carolina Herrera’s Miami flagship, a sculptural chandelier by artist Liz Oliver hangs suspended above a soft pink couch.

It has been revealed that in September, Carolina Herrera held an extravaganza of a runway show during New York Fashion Week, celebrating the brand’s 45th anniversary. This past week, the festivities went further south, to Miami. Last Thursday night, creative director Wes Gordon and members of the city’s fashion and arts community gathered beneath a cherry-red awning to toast the brand’s newest boutique—and sixth official location in the U.S.

Opened on August 15, the 3,000-square-foot shop sits in the middle of the Miami Design District, with a dramatic arched entrance welcoming guests into the limestone-finished structure. Designed in collaboration with interior designers Brandi Howe and Jessica Hyland of Hyland Studio, the store is bursting with color and feminine details—soft pink travertine covers the floor while furnishings feature red and pink accents. In the center of the main salon, a custom pink sofa with graceful curvature offers an elegant seat; in another area, the same red awning from the boutique’s entrance reappears suspended over a pair of regal armchairs.

“The Carolina Herrera woman is bold, elegant, and joyful. She embraces color, expresses herself with confidence, and never shies away from making an entrance,” states Gordon.

It has been revealed that but the fresh store is not only an ode to the Carolina Herrera brand but also to other female creatives. On view throughout the space are artworks commissioned specifically for the boutique as a part of the Carolina Herrera for Women in the Arts initiative. In the main salon, Los Angeles-based artist Liz Oliver designed a rose-colored textile installation that doubles as a sculptural chandelier. Elsewhere, ceramic planters made by the women-owned Choplet Ceramics are on display. Throughout the boutique, a recurring custom floral motif by Argentine artist Constanza Vallese appears on vases and tables.

In a recent development, in raising a glass to the boutique, guests at last Thursday’s event honored both the Carolina Herrera woman and her upcoming city. “Her energy is magnetic—much like the spirit of Miami,” notes Gordon. “It feels entirely natural that we should open our next home here.”.

  • It has been revealed that but what watch?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A watch is a sentimental gift. It’s not something casually given—not a tie or a fancy notebook or even a good pen or a nice bottle of booze. Don’t get me wrong, those are delightful things to receive and all appropriate for a run-of-the-mill holiday or birthday celebration. But some years aren’t run-of-the-mill. Some years require something extra. Some years are watch years—and trust me, you’ll know it when you get there.

It has been revealed that but what watch? It’s a personal choice, of course, but a personal choice that you’re making for someone else. Luckily, you likely know them pretty well. Around these parts, Esquire knows watches pretty well. Here are 12 suggestions, in price ranges from midwestern frugal to multigeneration inheritance. No matter how much you’re comfortable spending, you can’t go wrong with any of these watches.

Recent findings suggest that A classic watch for a classic guy. The Khaki Field Expedition is the quintessential field watch. Rich history of American craftsmanship, purpose-driven aesthetics, functional compass bezel (even if I can’t figure out how to use it for the life of me), and in the past few years it’s been available with the always practical NATO strap. It’s an ideal watch for the horologist, who’ll appreciate the history, the movement, and the exhibition case back. Win-win, guaranteed all-star gift.

I’m an unabashed Citizen fan. The Promaster “Fugu” is my favorite watch in the $500 range, and the Japanese brand’s Eco-Drive offerings are even more affordable. The Promaster Sea Eco-Drive is almost criminally underpriced for the watch that you get. We’re talking an emerald-green dial with a matching unidirectional 60-minute bezel, 200 meter depth rating, and a stainless-steel bracelet for well under $300. This is a great gift for the practically driven, classic dive-watch fan. And if the green dial is too swerve-y, the black and the blue are both excellent choices.

Industry observers note that good doesn’t always mean expensive. A major ol’ dive watch isn’t appropriate for every occasion or every guy. Simpler can be better. Like this under-$100 life-proof G-Shock. It treads the line between classic G-Shock aesthetics and little Casio reference. A watch equally appropriate for a man who never thinks about watches or one who is always thinking about watches—Schrödinger’s timepiece of no taste or good taste. And, hot take, it pairs better with a suit than sneakers do. Keep your shoes formal and let your watch carry the high-low combo.

Industry observers note that if he’s not a G-Shock man, he may be an Ironman. A Timex Ironman, that is, even if he’s not logging an insane amount of weekend mileage. As the world grows wary of increased technocracy-driven smart designs, there’s a simple nostalgia to the ’90s-tech runner’s watch. Turns out they were right all along. You don’t need a phone on your wrist, just a stopwatch and an alarm clock and a 100-lap memory to boot. I also like the orange accents here. If he is midwestern frugal and would object to a gift over $100, this scaled-back version also plays.

In a recent development, shinola’s Duck Watch references ’60s and ’70s skin divers, which sounds dirty but really is just a term for smaller, less depth-rated dive watches and the culture of free diving and spearfishing around them. That’s a reductive explanation that some watch nerds will quibble with, but it’ll serve us for now. The two crucial things to take away are 1) there was a magazine of the same name that you can find on eBay and 2) Shinola’s modern version is a killer watch. I have this one in Canary Yellow, but I recently borrowed the upcoming Mallard Brown colorway for a photo shoot, and I love it. Hated to send it back. In the sun, the dial turns almost iridescent, like the titular duck’s feathers. It’s battery powered, water-resistant, and not fussy at all.

[Editor’s note: The Mallard Brown colorway is currently out of stock, so for the time being we will direct you to the Canary.].

Industry observers note that let’s get fancy. But let’s get fancy with purpose. More on Rolexes soon, but I think Panerai makes the most exciting watches in the $5,000 to $15,000 range. I realize that’s a large range, one encompassing the price of a decent motorcycle or a used Camry, but I’m talking luxury Swiss-made watches here. This is the tip of the iceberg. Panerai has design panache and exquisite movements, a design that’s not too “look at me” but still far enough outside the classic mold that it demands a second look. It’s not a watch for everyone, but man, those who will love it will love it immensely.

Recently I hosted a friend and fellow style writer for a will-not-be-named rival publication at the Detroit headquarters of T-shirt maker Soft Goods MFG. He had a couple enviable pieces (understated Nitty Gritty corduroy jacket, Paraboot derbies, perfectly faded vintage Levi’s), but I kept looking at his watch, a Unimatic Quattro. In the interest of individuality and my own love of a good suede, I’m suggesting this Todd Snyder collab as the next gift for that extra-special man in your life. It’s Unimatic with a twist, Italian design with an Americana POV, like spaghetti western for your wrist. Clint Eastwood fans rejoice.

Timex and J. Crew’s recent trout-forward collab watch sold out in an instant—unfortunately before I could get my hands on one. But there are other options for the outdoorsy dude. Especially one who cares about stopping forest fires. This Vero Smokey Bear option toes the line between campy and classy with aplomb. It’ll look good while you’re chopping wood or a little Wes Anderson–y at the lodge with a glass of bourbon in hand, telling stories about the trout that got away.

It has been revealed that TAG can get a bad rap in the watch-collecting community, but ignore the critics, especially if your intended recipient is a racing enthusiast. TAG Heuer has a long history in F1 and Grand Prix, and it looks as much at home in the cockpit of a fancy Brad Pitt–piloted car as it does in the fan stands or the sports bar. If you want to step it up a level, the Monaco is a luxury take on a race-day watch—all European angles and rich leather.

In a recent development, this is the only pilot’s watch on the list—and for good reason. It’s the most handsome pilot’s watch on the market. Marathon developed these in partnership with the Kelly Air Force Base in 1986 and specced it out to withstand high-altitude flight, or even an ejection. If you’re in the market for a classic pilot’s chronograph, Bremont makes the best one. But if you are in the market for a no-frills, all-style, practically designed pilot’s watch, the Marathon Arctic Navigator is your ticket.

Sources indicate that maybe he’s a Rolex Pepsi guy, but you’re on a non-Swiss-made budget. I’ll let you in on a secret: Seiko makes a pretty damn good approximation. I particularly like that this one is PADI co-branded and automatic, with a 200 meter depth rating. Even better, it’s under $500.

According to recent reports, for my money, Doxa makes some of the most interesting dive watches out there. Is this on the list because I’d really love if someone took the hint and bought one for me? Hard to say. What’s easy to say is that the orange-dial Doxa Sub 200T is a showstopper. It’s got a slightly smaller profile and a more interesting silhouette than the original 200 but still retains the necessary details, like its unidirectional rotating bezel with its integrated U.S. Navy no-decompression limit table. No rules on whether that’s used underwater or just at the dinner table, either. It’s good to know how long to cook a steak for.

Spoilers ahead for The Body season 1.

Sources indicate that talk about divine intervention. Now that you’ve finished the first season of The Body, let’s talk about that ending. Specifically, what happens to Grace? Is she alive? Is she somehow more than that? How?!

Recent findings suggest that at the beginning of the first season, Sofia Wylie’s character Grace is initiated into the dance team and given drugs at a house party as part of a “Satanic ritual.” The drug, ecstasy, causes Grace to pass out, seize, and seemingly die that night. The party took place at a building called Devil’s House... what did they expect? The girls try to cover up what they did by driving her home. But then, unexpectedly, Grace starts breathing again at the end of the episode. Is Grace just in a coma? That’s what they go with until things get weirder. It kind of becomes a whole thing.

Well, it was 2004. The Passion of the Christ was one of the highest-grossing films of the year. Everyone was doing the Numa Numa dance and just starting to get into Lost. If a teenage girl came back from the dead, it would be a huge deal. People would definitely try to cast her as a savior, which is what happens to Grace.

Recent findings suggest that lisbeth starts claiming she tried to resuscitate her, and that her survival is a miracle she performed. Meanwhile, Grace starts haunting some of the girls in their dreams. So, naturally, they start to ascribe meaning to her. Word spreads, and before long the whole town starts to worship.

It has been revealed that in the finale, immediately after Anya confesses to what they did, Grace wakes up from her coma and says “I’m God.” She is risen? Literally, that’s what she says. (It’s also, for the theory-brained, the same thing Lisbeth says when she reveals up at the infamous Halloween party because she dressed up as “slutty God,” complete with a toga and a giant crucifix. You know, just before she talks about being anointed.).

What did she mean by that? Does she even realize that she said it? Not only are Grace’s words bizarre, but doctors also conclude that she wasn’t even in a coma that whole time. All they’re able to conclude is that she was unconscious. Where was she?! What happened to her?!

According to Wylie, creator Quinn Shepherd has an explanation that the two of them are keeping to themselves for potential future seasons of The Body. “Quinn’s explanation is something I’d love to keep under wraps,” the actress told Tudum, “because I think the beauty of the show is that it stays within the mystery, whether it’s medical or spiritual.”.

It has been revealed that so, ultimately, it’s all a significant mystery. We just have to have faith that The Body will get renewed for season 2 and continue this story.

Senate Republicans lament midterms, weigh leadership election delay

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Senate Majority Leader John Thune arrives for a GOP conference meeting at the Capitol on Tuesday.
  • Senate Republicans on Tuesday were weighing whether to postpone their leadership elections after what several senators described as a “frank” conversation about their midterm losses last week.
  • But so far, no official candidate has emerged to challenge John Thune, R-S.D., for the post of minority leader in the new Congress.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senate Majority Leader John Thune arrives for a GOP conference meeting at the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Republicans on Tuesday were weighing whether to postpone their leadership elections after what several senators described as a “frank” conversation about their midterm losses last week.

But so far, no official candidate has emerged to challenge John Thune, R-S.D., for the post of minority leader in the new Congress.

The conference was supposed to begin its leadership elections Tuesday morning, but pushed those back to hear from members still reeling from the midterm results, which saw the GOP lose their Senate majority. As the conference meeting turned into what some dubbed an “open-mic session,” they took a break to attend previously scheduled committee hearings, with a proposal to return at 2 p.m. Next they must decide whether to forge ahead and pick leaders Tuesday or to punt those choices to a different day.

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., noted the conversation taking place was “honest” and “frank.”.

It has been revealed that “I will vote for the delay,” he said. “We’ve got a lot of things that we’ve got to think through, and I think to rush into this and to just ratify all the same leadership — I mean, what message does that send?”.

“If you don’t think after losing seven seats minimum that we need to change course, I don’t know what planet you’re on,” he stated, adding he was frustrated that his party didn’t do more to focus on topics like affordability ahead of the midterms. “I know it’s easy to blame other people, but we need to look at what has happened here.”.

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., who is leading the charge to delay the leadership elections and collected signatures to call the conference meeting beforehand, called it “a very high-quality conversation” in which he was “leading.”.

“People are voicing opinions on all sides of the issues. It’s one of those times in the Republican conference where you kind of go, ‘We’ve got some smart people, and we’re having a very good, respectful conversation.’”.

No challenger to Thune, the current majority leader, stepped forward during the closed-door meeting, several senators said. Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., said “they’re not even criticizing Thune” inside the room. “It hasn’t been about John Thune.”.

“It’s been about the family,” Cramer remarked, describing it as a “family discussion.” Thune and others in leadership had yet to speak, as the candidate forum hadn’t started yet.

According to recent reports, sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., remarked voters reacted to high gas prices, the war in Iran and the cost of living.

“The cost of living defeated us,” Paul said. “I don’t think anybody in Texas who voted for the Democrat governor was voting against John Thune. If you diagnose that as a problem, you’re misdiagnosing the problem.”.

Hawley didn’t say how long he’d like to see a delay. “Long enough for people to think through this, and if there’s somebody else … or several somebodies who want to run for positions, let them think through it.”.

Cramer was asked if senators in the room were placing any blame on President Donald Trump over how he handled midterm messaging.

“There was a lot of discussion about the president,” Cramer remarked.

Sources indicate that john M. Donnelly contributed to the report.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that that’s not to say that filmmakers aren’t trying.
  • In a recent development, you won’t find a Thanksgiving movie list without Planes, Trains and Automobiles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that most people don’t think of Thanksgiving when they think of holiday movies. Halloween and Christmas? of course. Valentine’s Day? You bet! But outside of John Hughes’s 1987 comedy Planes, Trains and Automobiles starring Steve Martin and John Candy, Hollywood still struggles to really capture the feeling of Thanksgiving on film.

Sources indicate that that’s not to say that filmmakers aren’t trying. The thirty films below capture all the fall vibes, family squabbles, and strenuous meal planning that come with Thanksgiving dinner—even if some of them don’t technically take place on Thanksgiving. (Still, I tried my best to keep those at a minimum.) If you’re looking for something to watch with the whole family, start an argument, or just feel thankful that good Thanksgiving movies do exist, these are the Thanksgiving movies that are actually worth watching.

In a recent development, you won’t find a Thanksgiving movie list without Planes, Trains and Automobiles. The 1987 John Hughes comedy is a genuine classic—arguably so good that no one’s made a better Thanksgiving film since. How could they? The story follows a marketing executive (played by Steve Martin) who just wants to get home to New York for Thanksgiving on the busiest travel day of the year. Instead, he spends the entire three-day trip across the country with a chatty shower ring salesman (John Candy). Despite Martin’s prickliness, they’re forced to bond over the holiday while sharing the kind of heartfelt laughs that most movies nowadays just can’t replicate with the same sincerity anymore.

In a recent development, this is one of the movies that that you’ll see on the list that is more about fall than it is about Thanksgiving, but You’ve Got Mail does include a Thanksgiving scene. In this 1998 romantic comedy starring Tom Hanks and Meg Ryan and written and directed by Nora and Delia Ephron, two Upper West Side New Yorkers meet in an online chat room and fall in love over a series of months. At one point, Tom Hanks walks into Zabar's on Thanksgiving, which is maybe the most New York thing one can do.

In a recent development, jodie Foster's finest directorial effort remains this 1995 comedy about the Thanksgiving get-together of Holly Hunter's thoroughly dysfunctional clan, which includes her mother (Anne Bancroft) and father (Charles Durning), her brother (Robert Downey Jr.), and his friend (Dylan McDermott). What ensues is the gold standard for family-gathering holiday films, full of absurdity, pathos, and ultimately a rousing sense of the ups and downs of dealing with relatives.

Industry observers note that an ensemble cast of Vanessa Williams, Vivica A. Fox, Nia Long, and Michael Beach star in this comedy-drama film about a Black American family that gets together every Sunday to have dinner. But when Significant Mama (Irma P. Hall) falls ill, her three daughters’ strained relationships take on an entirely new form. While the meals never occur on Thanksgiving Day, the family arguments over a mouth-watering meal do.

Remember the Titans isn't technically a Thanksgiving movie either. But it features plenty of those Thanksgiving elements—football, fall foliage, and large amounts of people gathering for meals. The film stars Denzel Washington as a high school football coach who is brought in to teach at a predominately white school in Alexandria, Virginia. And if it’s not playing on cable on Thanksgiving anyway—that is, if you haven’t cut the cord yet—I’m sure a streaming service picked it up for the holiday.

Recent findings suggest that maybe it's not as iconic as A Charlie Brown Christmas or It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown, but this Peanuts holiday special is a good holdover between Halloween and Christmas. This Emmy-winning classic sees Peppermint Patty infiltrating Charlie Brown's Thanksgiving holiday, which he naturally scrambles to put together with his trademark anxiety. (Where the hell are these kids' parents, by the way?).

Spike Lee's iconic She's Gotta Have It, following one woman's love square with her three competing lovers, isn't typically included in the wholesome holiday canon. But few films have featured a more memorable Thanksgiving dinner than that of Nola Darling (Tracy Camilla Johns), in which she invites over all three men to celebrate the holiday together as she sits at the head of the table.

Opening and closing with scenes of its characters at Thanksgiving dinner, Woody Allen's 1986 comedic drama—which won him an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay and Best Supporting Actor and Actress statuettes for Michael Caine and Dianne Wiest, respectively—tells a raft of interconnected stories, all in some way related to Mia Farrow's Hannah and her two siblings. Equal parts hilarious and touching, it remains one of the writer-director's crowning achievements.

According to recent reports, it’s not the holidays if you haven’t watched a Lifetime movie with the family yet. Still, that doesn’t mean you must subject yourself to the most baseless shlock. How about a simple, magic family film from the creator of the Muppets. Well, posthumously, that is. And yes, that means puppets—but that should only be a plus!

In a recent development, knives Out just screams cozy with all of its sweaters, wooden decorations, and fallen leaves. Rian Johnson's mystery flick, which is now a trilogy, is a must-watch if you're in a family that loves solving puzzles or escape rooms (or, you know, Daniel Craig). Hopefully, your Thanksgiving isn’t anywhere near as chaotic.

Sources indicate that okay, so, technically this would be more faithful to the Thanksgiving canon if it were Turkey Run. But this feature-film debut from the iconic Aardman animation studio is a Thanksgiving hit for obvious reasons. The stop-motion film, centered on a group of chickens determined to escape execution before being turned into chicken pies, is as hilarious as it is visually spectacular.

Sources indicate that christmas Vacation is in a category of its own, but the entire National Lampoon franchise is usually a crowd-pleaser at family holidays. This one features Malcolm in the Middle–era Bryan Cranston as the eccentric hippie and long-lost cousin of suburban man Mitch Snider. Awkward family antics ensue.

For the Christopher Guest and Eugene Levy fans, this 2006 mockumentary is about three actors played by Guest favorites Catherine O’Hara, Parker Posey, and Harry Shearer, who are making a film called Home for Purim, which is supposedly garnering lots of Oscar buzz. Things come to a bit of a halt when the studio intervenes and renames the film Home for Thanksgiving, changing the entire plot of the film just to chase awards.

In a recent development, this movie jumps around to four different Thanksgiving meals, all thrown by families from diverse backgrounds who have a few things in common: stress, food, and stressing over food. What’s Cooking? also features an ensemble cast composed of Kyra Sedgwick, Joan Chen, Lainie Kazan, Mercedes Ruehl, Maury Chaykin, Julianna Margulies, Alfre Woodard, and Dennis Haysbert.

For a little switch-up, this one is a documentary. Directed by Martin Scorsese, this film follows The Band’s Thanksgiving farewell show, featuring Joni Mitchell, Bob Dylan, and Eric Clapton. Alongside Stop Making Sense, The Last Waltz is often cited as one of the greatest music concert films ever made.

Many films in the ‘40s concerned the difficulties soldiers faced when coming home from the war, but few attempted to bring our heroes home over Thanksgiving. The Very Thought of You, which is more of a romantic drama, stars Dennis Morgan and Dane Clark as they return just for the holiday—before they’re shipped back once the weekend ends. Fair warning: This one’s a bit of a tear-jerker. “You know those advertisements that show pictures of guys in uniform coming back to what they left?,” one character says in the film. “They don’t show what home really means.”.

It has been revealed that thanksgiving is anything but jovial in Ang Lee's The Ice Storm, which is set around the holiday in 1973 Connecticut, where two well-off families struggle with all manner of the-times-they-are-a'-changin' upheaval. Adultery and alcohol inevitably play a massive factor in their problems, which are dramatized by director Lee—and handled by his cast, including Kevin Kline, Joan Allen, Sigourney Weaver, Tobey Maguire, Christina Ricci, and Elijah Wood—with chilling incisiveness.

In a recent development, in her finest performance, Katie Holmes plays the titular April, who bravely invites her dysfunctional family from suburban Pennsylvania to her tiny apartment on the Lower East Side. Disaster strikes early when her stove breaks and she is forced to find a working oven in her building. Meanwhile, her cancer-stricken mother (Oscar nominee Patricia Clarkson) slowly dreads the trek into the city to see her somewhat estranged daughter.

Sources indicate that on Thanksgiving 1983, Marty (Josh Hamilton) brings his fiancée Lesly (Parker Posey) home to meet his family—his dim-witted and horny brother, Anthony; his cold and nosey mother, Mrs. Pascal; and his mentally unhinged and Kennedy-obsessed sister, Jackie-O. All hell breaks loose, naturally, as kitchen knives are hidden, sexual boundaries are tested, and Parker Posey delivers one of the most hilariously intense performances of her career.

In a recent development, judd Apatow's dramatic comedy stars Adam Sandler as George Simmons, a wealthy movie star who seeks to get back to his stand-up-comedy roots after being diagnosed with leukemia. He meets a young aspiring comic (Seth Rogen) in search of a mentor, and the two tour the country as George performs his upcoming material and reconnects with his ex-fiancée. It's a film about the comedy world and how friendships evolve into familial relationships, highlighted by a Thanksgiving toast George delivers in honor of his chosen family.

Sources indicate that trey Edward Shults made his directorial debut with this indie drama, which stars members of his real-life family—including his aunt Krisha Fairchild in the titular role. Krisha arrives at her sister's house for a Thanksgiving celebration after years of estrangement from her family. Overwhelmed by her return to this seemingly normal life, Krisha starts drinking and popping pills in secret—and all hell breaks loose as emotions fly and family secrets are exposed.

Much like Krisha above, The Humans is for people who really can’t stand Thanksgiving. Based on Stephen Karam’s Tony Award-winning play, the film stars a family played by Richard Jenkins, Jayne Houdyshell, Amy Schumer, Beanie Feldstein, Steven Yeun, and June Squibb as they all just tear into each other over Thanksgiving dinner.

According to recent reports, this sequel to the big-screen adaptation of the classic TV sitcom finds the spooky-ooky Addams family once again up to their weird, gothic ways. But their family is thrown into turmoil when a fresh nanny, Debbie (a pitch-perfect Joan Cusack), has her sights on Uncle Fester—and plans on marrying him for his riches before killing him off. Wednesday and Pugsley know something's up, but Debbie convinces Gomez and Morticia to send them to summer camp—where they are forced to participate in a completely bonkers musical rendition of the first Thanksgiving.

Sources indicate that folk rocker Arlo Guthrie (son of Woody) plays himself in this offbeat comedy film inspired by his song of the same name. Guthrie, a long-haired draft dodger visiting some friends in an uptight Massachusetts town for Thanksgiving, thinks he's doing his hosts a favor by filling his Volkswagen minibus with their garbage and taking it to the dump. A mix-up ensues, Guthrie is busted for littering, and he seeks to prove himself unfit for combat when the draft comes calling.

Nobody's Fool is one of the last great headlining vehicles for Paul Newman, who stars here as an upstate New York construction-worker hustler in constant conflict with a contractor (Bruce Willis) whose wife (Melanie Griffith) he fancies. His routine is upended by the arrival of his estranged son (Dylan Walsh) around Thanksgiving, leading to an amusing (and disarming) holiday-set character study about loneliness, reconciliation, and the unexpected ways people achieve contentment.

Sources indicate that over the course of a Thanksgiving weekend, Chris O'Donnell's prep-school student comes of age while caring for a blind retired Army lieutenant (Al Pacino) in Martin Brest's acclaimed Scent of a Woman, which finally earned Pacino his first-ever Academy Award (for Best Actor). Amid all of its star's blustery hoo-ahing, it's a surprisingly tender tale of an unlikely friendship between two strangers.

Jack Lemmon and Walter Matthau are two bitter lifelong rivals who engage in ludicrous warfare over the affections of the new resident (Ann-Margret) of their Wabasha, Minnesota, neighborhood. That conflict includes an amusing Thanksgiving dinner, in which the two do their best to act like feuding, immature children.

Another cozy classic. Wes Anderson’s stop-motion film about a family of foxes with a killer voice cast—George Clooney, Meryl Streep, Jason Schwartzman, Bill Murray, Wilem Dafoe, Owen Wilson, Brian Cox, and Adrien Brody—couldn’t be a better film to watch with your family this holiday.

There’s never been a Thanksgiving-based superhero that I can recall—nor should there be—but the original Spider-Man film with Tobey Maguire features a particularly memorable Thanksgiving scene. Peter’s Aunt May invites the Osbornes over for Thanksgiving when Norman (Willem Dafoe) notices one of Peter’s injuries and deduces that he’s Spider-Man.

Eli Roth turned an actual joke project into a feature film in 2023 when he released Thanksgiving, a Halloween-esque slasher horror film about a killer let loose on Turkey Day. He wears a John Carver mask, carries an axe, and absolutely hates Black Friday. On the latter, we can all agree.

Her name? Her name is Bella Hadid, and it seems she has a upcoming man in her life. Oh, and he just so happens to be another cowboy. What can we say? Our girl Bella has a type, and she’s incredibly real for that!

The cowboy in question is Nathan Lacy, who she has been reportedly linked to since March 2026. They first sparked dating rumors when he was spotted trailing behind her during Milan Fashion Week, and now, they seemingly hard-debuted at the boy aquarium a hockey game.

Industry observers note that for the most part, Bella and Nathan have kept their romance out of the spotlight, but if you want to know how they met and when things started getting ~ romantic ~, you’ve come to the right place. Scroll through Bella Hadid and Nathan Lacy’s low-key relationship timeline ahead.

Before she started dating Nathan, Bella was linked to a different professional horseman: Adan Banuelos. The pair reportedly met at a horse show in Fort Worth, Texas, and dated for more than two years before calling it quits due to long distance and scheduling conflicts in early 2026.

Recent findings suggest that “Bella is doing her best to stay positive and distract herself since their split,” a source told Entertainment Weekly at the time. “She's been staying busy with work and spending time with close friends. She is still processing the breakup since it was a very serious relationship."⁠.

A source for Us Weekly unveiled that Adan and Bella were back together after a “brief but needed” split.

Sources indicate that per the insider, “They are working on their relationship right now. He has been a huge part of her life in Texas, so it’s been hard for her to let go.”.

It has been revealed that amid Adan reconciliation rumors, Bella sparked romance rumors with yet another cowboy after Nathan was spotted walking with her during Milan Fashion Week. He was later identified as her friend Rachael Lacy’s brother, though neither addressed speculation about their relationship at that point.

Sources indicate that to make matters about her relationship status a little confusing, Bella was spotted with Adan at a cutting event hosted at Taylor Sheridan’s ranch in Texas. A source told TMZ that they were still together and had never officially broken up. Um…what?

It has been revealed that bella spent time with both Adan and Nathan in Colorado, further complicating speculation about her love life. First, she hung out with Adan in Aspen, according to Deuxmoi.

But then, Rachael snuck a pic of Bella and Nathan in her photo dump posted on July 16:.

An insider told the Daily Mail that she was getting to know someone new but wasn’t looking for anything serious, while TMZ later reported that Bella was single and dating neither man.

Bella and Nathan were spotted grocery shopping together in Crested Butte, Colorado, over Labor Day weekend, per pics obtained by Deuxmoi.

Bella seemingly gave fans a clue about her relationship status in an Instagram photo dump following the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show.

Eagle-eyed followers noticed what appeared to be a photo of her kissing Nathan on her phone’s lock screen. What’s more: She deleted the pic from her dump shortly after.

After months of back-and-forth and a bunch of questions surrounding their relationship status, Bella and Nathan seemingly hard-released their relationship during a Colorado Avalanche hockey game on November 7.

Bella also went Instagram official with Nathan, posting cute selfies from the game in her photo dump.

A day later, on November 18, they were photographed packing on PDA in Aspen.

Then Bella’s cover story with Harper’s Bazaar dropped, and—though she didn’t reference Nathan by name—she did talk about her dream of “living in peace, in a small town, with a man that I love, with my child, having my animals.”.

6 Stylish Ways to Wear a Blanket Coat This Fall and Winter

  • Blanket coats have become the cold-weather item fashion people are loving, and it was all over a lot of the fall/winter 2026 runways, too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that beating the cold has gotten that much easier with the rise of blanket coats. This winter, we’re staying bundled up, not only with stylish layering tricks like wraps, shawls, and capes, but by blending the two.

Blanket coats have become the cold-weather item fashion people are loving, and it was all over a lot of the fall/winter 2026 runways, too. So, it’s clear that the style is making the rounds, and there’s no need to wait for next winter to finally be tuned in. Blanket coats provide the coziness of at-home comfort, snuggled beneath a good quilt, to your everyday outfits.

It has been revealed that and most serve a two-in-one purpose, also providing some neck protection, so you can opt out of scarves sometimes, or double up if you’re dealing with some really cold days. Below, I’ve gathered some stylish ways to lean into the popular blanket coat trend this fall and winter.

If you’re looking for something that feels a bit elevated, try a blanket coat similar to this style with draping that bunches and gathers flawlessly, giving an almost regal vibe.

In a recent development, if you’re not big on layering, let the coat do the layering for you. Leaning into a blanket jacket like this one that’s split open at the front makes it look like you’re wearing more pieces than you actually are.

The blanket coat serves as a literal wrap-around sweater that keeps you cozy and stylish. This black with brown trim one is perfect for your every day.

It has been revealed that while some blanket coats wrap, others fall like trenches, but carry a bit thicker material like the one above. Pairing a simple neutral-colored piece with a monotone outfit is the easy way in.

In a recent development, the best part of a good blanket style coat is that it keeps you covered without having to deal with a zipper. If you want a more relaxed-fit coat then a style like this is great.

For those days when you wish you could carry around a significant blanket with you, try instead pulling out your thickest coat that gives all the vibes.

She is an award-winning journalist from Miami, Florida, and a graduate of the historically Black university, Florida A&M. She is a 2024 Forbes 30 Under 30: Media honoree, and her debut romance novella PASSING GAME is set to release March of 2027 (831 Stories/Simon & Schuster).

Winter Essentials Worth Giving—and Keeping

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor.
  • It’s an oft-expressed sentiment, but it’s true: The holidays turn people’s attention toward friends, family, and community.
  • Whether you equate The North Face with everyday city wear or outdoor adventures, it’s a solid, time-tested spot to get a gift for a loved one (or yourself).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every product was carefully curated by an Esquire editor. We may earn a commission from these links. Here’s how we test products and why you should trust us.

It’s an oft-expressed sentiment, but it’s true: The holidays turn people’s attention toward friends, family, and community. There’s a beauty in the selfless, caring gifts people give to others. And while all that giving feels great, the holidays are also a good time to treat yourself. Plus, it’s getting colder.

Whether you equate The North Face with everyday city wear or outdoor adventures, it’s a solid, time-tested spot to get a gift for a loved one (or yourself). The brand has jackets and accessories with familiar winter looks, as well as products with less expected silhouettes that still offer protection from the elements in an understated style.

Here’s a look at some of the best cold-weather gear that will have you wrapping up the gift of warmth and durability… even if that gift is for yourself.

This is an easy gifting win because the warm, hooded, insulated jacket is a recognizable The North Face staple, evoking an unpretentious spin on the brand’s iconic Nuptse Jacket.

It’s familiar, but it’s also practical—the kind of gift you feel good about because it’s going to get a ton of use. (And it can withstand the repeated wears.) The attached hood offers protection from biting winds, and the straightforward color options make it easy to pair with a variety of outfits, whether it’s something fun or part of a heavy bundling during the coldest days of winter. This is the perfect type of winter coat: warm but not too puffy.

The Zaneck Jacket is a great alternative to the Aconcagua, stepping away from the outdoorsy look the brand is best known for. It’s still waterproof and insulated, but it has a longer, more modern cut.

The Zaneck comes with a removable faux fur lining for the hood, which, in addition to being warm, means there are a couple of different looks that can be teased out of it. The straight cuffs add to its stylish feel in a way that doesn’t scream “I’m dressed for warmth and not fashion,” even though it’s doing both.

The Lone Peak Triclimate 2 has a lot in common with the Zaneck. From a distance, they cut a similar silhouette. However, the Lone Peak adds a little versatility if you’re looking for a jacket that can handle a variety of climates.

A removable, insulated inner jacket is attached to a removable, insulated top layer, which is fit for rainy conditions or as a spring or fall jacket. The insulated layer converts the whole thing into a winter-ready jacket. It also sports underarm vents capable of releasing heat in the middle of a long hike, ideal for outdoorsy types. The hood is removable and it’s got adjustable cuffs and an adjustable hem, making this a do-it-all jacket.

It might be easy to ignore the Pertex Jacket. It’s a bit unassuming. It doesn’t cut as stylish of a figure as the Zaneck, but it’s endlessly useful. The lightweight Pertex fabric will keep you dry in a downpour, but it also offers warmth without marshmallow-like bulk.

The lightweight aspect makes this the kind of coat you toss in the backseat on the way to a hike, just in case. It’s also great for layering, whether it’s tossed on over a sweater or layered under an overcoat to make a favorite jacket more winter-ready.

Industry observers note that this edition of the classic Base Camp Duffel echoes the design details we love in The North Face’s jackets. While it’s got enough style and a heap of color options for daily use, it’s built for adventure.

Made with water- and tear-resistant fabric, it boasts 71 liters of storage space, a roomier option to the similar 31-liter version. Like all of the brand’s products, it’s built as if the designers have been through the rigors of outdoor adventures (and they probably have). It’s got a sweeping D-zip opening, backpack straps, mesh pockets, and compression straps in case you’re curious if you can pack 73 liters worth of gear into the 71-liter space. (You know you’ve tried.).

The North Face has a lot of hats, none more iconic than this. The Salty Lined Beanie has a classic feel, fitting snuggly over the head with rib-knit texture, a cuffed shape, soft fabric, and ample color options to ensure it will match any jacket or accessory. The Salty Lined Beanie encapsulates the entire The North Face vibe in a small way: It’s stylish enough for a subway ride to work and practical enough for an outdoor adventure. Best of all, it’ll keep your ears warm in either instance.

Often, the best glove is the one that disappears into the outfit. It looks seamless, keeping hands warm without drawing too much attention. The Etip Recycled Glove is about functionality first and foremost, but the simple design and understated colors makes it look good with a variety of winter outfits.

While we all like to pretend we aren’t attached to our phones, the Etip makes a great modern gift because its stretchy fleece delivers a snug fit and the palms have touchscreen compatibility. That means you won’t have to take off your gloves to respond to that crucial text while the snow is falling.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that chair Teresa Leger Fernández, D-N.M., conducts a news conference with members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus during a 2025 retreat in Leesburg, Va.
  • The leaders of an effort to overhaul how the House deals with sexual misconduct hope their proposal will see action before the end of the 119th Congress, though they’re split on the odds.
  • Kat Cammack, R-Fla., chair of the Republican Women’s Caucus, noted legislative text is done and is being looked at by the relevant committees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that chair Teresa Leger Fernández, D-N.M., conducts a news conference with members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus during a 2025 retreat in Leesburg, Va. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

The leaders of an effort to overhaul how the House deals with sexual misconduct hope their proposal will see action before the end of the 119th Congress, though they’re split on the odds.

Sources indicate that rep. Kat Cammack, R-Fla., chair of the Republican Women’s Caucus, noted legislative text is done and is being looked at by the relevant committees.

“Yes, absolutely,” she said when asked if the package would get a vote this year. “We’re shopping it now with the different committees, House Admin and Ethics, and waiting on their final feedback, which we should have actually this week.”.

Sources indicate that rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, said she was still optimistic about getting it done, but stopped short of putting full faith in Republican leadership to get it over the finish line. The effort has been underway since May, when Cammack and Leger Fernández’s caucuses confirmed a partnership to propose changes after two members of the House resigned amid allegations of sexual misconduct.

Asked if she thought Speaker Mike Johnson would put the proposal on the floor during the busy lame-duck session, Leger Fernández laughed.

“Hopefully, that’s something that will happen, because you know the Republican Women’s Caucus had said they were optimistic before we left. I’m still optimistic,” she said.

Sources indicate that the two groups have spent months holding dozens of meetings with staff, their own caucuses and male members of Congress, among others. Suggestions have included banning members of Congress from engaging in sexual relationships with any House staffer, not just those who work for them directly, and outlining penalties for violaters. Initially, the groups were expected to unveil their work by August recess, but that got pushed back as the House canceled weeks in session and as they cited a desire to get it right.

Cammack said she thinks Johnson “has been very sincere in his efforts on this.”.

Sources indicate that “That would be a tremendous disappointment” if he didn’t put it on the floor, she remarked when asked about the possibility. “I genuinely believe he cares about this concern.”.

Leger Fernández stated if it doesn’t get done by the end of the 119th Congress, she hopes some changes would be adopted under the rules package for the next Congress that Democrats bring forward in January. Such packages are typically adopted with party-line votes and give incoming majorities the chance to tweak how the House operates to their liking. While certain narrower proposals aimed at curbing sexual harassment could be written into House rules, others would need to pass both chambers and be enacted into law to take effect.

In a recent development, “We are going to move to make sure it is in the rules package, because we will be in charge next year,” Leger Fernández remarked. “But I would love for it to pass now, because that was a commitment that it be bipartisan.”.

Sources indicate that last Thursday, and on a bipartisan basis, the Senate approved the so-called Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), an alleged effort to “reform” the federal permitting process for things like energy projects, hard-rock mining, and, yes, data centers. At the very least, the bill lived up to one part of its clumsy title; its passage through the Senate truly was bipartisan. It passed by a 62–33 vote, and liberal Democratic senator Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island was one of its strongest advocates.

It’s also a very massive apple with more than a few razor blades concealed inside. Environmentalists have been giving BAAJA the side-eye for a number of reasons. Out in Nebraska, Democratic state chair Jane Fleming Kleeb suspects the bill is connected to a sudden revival of interest in restarting our old friend, the Keystone XL pipeline, the continent-spanning death funnel meant to bring the world’s dirtiest fossil fuel from Alberta ultimately to refineries around the world.

My problem with this whole thing is that this “kind of civil war” is taking place exclusively on the Left. Conservative Republicans, and their oligarchical allies, are forcing the action before the new Democratic majorities take over in January. They know exactly what they want out of the bill and what they don’t want in it. The president already has noted there won’t be any wind farms under the provisions of this bill on his watch. (The birds! The whales!) The bill now is with the House of Representatives. May I suggest a discreet dragging of the feet? It is the holiday season, after all.
