Recent findings suggest that cecilie Bahnsen has a cult following for a reason: the Danish designer’s big blooming dresses and dedication to sporty, easy balletcore have been collected in droves by fashion far and wide. So when Uniqlo came calling for her to design a second collaboration, it was time again for the designer to take the reins and merge her playful girlish Scandi style with the utilitarian wearability of the Japanese giant. The collection, which includes womenswear and childrenswear, puts a focus on cozy winter wardrobe dressing and is available now. In it, Bahnsen is rethinking and retooling the classic winter fleece.

In a recent development, for the occasion, Bahnsen spent half a year designing the collection and also collaborated with her friend Fumiko Imano, the artist, to shoot the campaign in Sweden amidst a picturesque landscape. “It was very much about sisterhood, the journey you do of exploring together, and inspiration also from when I’m in the countryside with my son, and we collect flowers, and how we kind of, he sometimes pinned them on his jumper,” Bahnsen tells ELLE of the newly introduced collection. “I think it was really kind of that romantic or nostalgic feeling that I wanted to put into the collection. And then there was also this notion of just working with one fabrication and working with the fleece for winter and how you can work this as layering.”.

According to recent reports, while Bahnsen in particular is known for her flouncy babydoll dresses, when it came to her second collection for Uniqlo, she tells us it was all about “refinement and balance and creating beautiful kind of everyday pieces.” Her personal favorite piece of the lineup is the fleece in the palest shade of soft pastel pink, embroidered with small flowers. “For me, the fleece is such a classic layering piece,” she says. She’s already been wearing it herself for countryside outings. “There’s romance and nostalgia to pink, and I think with this collaboration, it was nice to do the fleece in pink,” she says. “Showing that it could have that femininity to it was special, and it is also that right tone as a super soft pink that I love.”.

According to recent reports, the entire collection is designed to be layered, and the fleece is at the center of it. There’s a cropped fleece vest, a sheer long T-shirt printed with subtle bouquets of flowers, a floral-embellished fleece skirt and matching socks, gloves, and hats. Bahnsen herself recommends taking a cue from her own runway highlights. “I always love a big jumper or a big fleece over a poof-y dress,” she says. “It has both a super boyish vibe to it but also a princess-y, romantic feeling, too, so I love those kinds of contrasts between each other.”.

Recent findings suggest that “These are pieces that you want to not just to work for one season, but to be timeless; it’s become about the perfection of these small details that makes it unique and maybe more romantic than what is normally in the Uniqlo collection,” adds Bahnsen. “I feel like the palette has a really Scandinavian winter tone to it, so how do you balance this soft pink into the darker blacks and blues, and kind of build it up, not in a monocomatic way, but really putting the tones and the layering together.” It’s definitely a chicer way to stay warm. The designer’s latest is the ultimate study of form and function.

You’ve manifested several milestones—job, apartment, a squad of ride-or-dies. Now, you need a way to get from one to the other. This is where State Farm comes in as your trusted partner to help you make informed decisions. Here’s what you’ll need to know before you enter your car owner era.

As images of weekend getaways and road trips with your besties fill your mind, so, too, should these pre-purchase considerations.

Sources indicate that at the dealership, put on your negotiation face. Buying a car is a little like dating—you do need to be observant, but you shouldn’t put all your cards (in this case: your budget) on the table. Finally, don’t be afraid to walk away. Follow these tips to make sure you're setting yourself up for success.

It has been revealed that before you turn up your favorite song and hit the open road, make sure your latest baby is protected. It can be a lot to take in, so let’s demystify insurance. Here’s what you need to know.

Rate: This is the baseline estimated price that would cover the potential cost of future claims. It’s determined using shared group factors such as age group; if you’re in your twenties, it would take into account the statistical driving information for other 25-year-olds in a region.

It has been revealed that premium: This is the adjusted individual insurance price that you’ll pay over a six- or 12-month period. It’s created by starting with the rate, then adding more specific factors that affect your claim risk level. These include your driving record, claims history, mileage usage, and vehicle type.

In a recent development, overwhelmed? Don’t sweat it—State Farm can get you an insurance quote before you buy.

Ah, the eternal question. Are you commitment-minded or more of a free agent?

To answer that when it comes to car ownership, consider how much you drive annually (to avoid leasing mileage overages if you exceed the stated mileage), how long you plan to keep your vehicle, and your financial situation.

Recent findings suggest that then, know that there are insurance differences between leasing and buying, too. Leasing companies adhere to stricter requirements than those that most states set, which could translate into higher monthly premiums.

If you buy to avoid the mileage caps and wear-and-tear of leasing, but still want the benefits of a fresh ride every few years, there is a moment during your payment plan when you can get a fresh car. Your initial loan payments largely go to interest (what lenders charge for giving you money), but there’s a break-even point when your payments begin going to principal (the actual amount you’ve borrowed). When that happens, and the outstanding balance is equal to the value of the car, you can trade it in for that amount, which is a budget-friendly way to upgrade.

Whatever you choose, a little strategy will keep you in the driver’s seat from dreaming about your new car to signing on the dotted line.

State Farm is there to protect you and your car.

#169186. What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1007 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

What’s a Vintage Car Rally Really Like? Inside the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run.

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1007 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor.
  • Gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp.
  • Venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In vintage rally driving, there are generally two types of competitor. Both share a passion for keeping priceless and nearly century-old vehicles in use on the open road rather than displaying them under glass. But some see the drive itself as challenge enough, while stalwarts adhere to what’s called the road book. This is a hundred or so pages of complex navigational directions that the copilot uses to navigate instead of a map, maintaining a constant flow of instructions to the driver. It is this book and how closely you follow it that decides the eventual winner.

Gianandrea Redaelli, a car nut whose family has long roots in the Italian printing business, is firmly in the “road book” camp. In early September, I climbed into the copilot seat of his 1939 Aston Martin C-Type Speed Model Roadster Bertelli—just one of two ever built, with an experimental aerodynamic body that earned it the nickname “the Flying Pea”—and stayed there as he drove six hundred kilometers of “left at the traffic lights, right at the cow” for the Louis Vuitton Dolomites Classic Run. The rally started in Venice and ended, after a scenic but challenging detour high into the Dolomite mountains, at Monza, the home of Italian Formula 1, just in time for practice day of the Grand Prix.

Venice might not seem the most logical starting line for a car rally given the proverbial wetness of the streets. But the city was chosen this year because it was also the end point of the last LV rally of its kind: the La Serenissima Run from Monte Carlo to Venice in 2012. Gianandrea won that one as copilot, with his father, Giuseppe, at the wheel. The pair also won the one before it—the Boheme across Hungary, the Czech Republic, and Austria—in 2006. This time, however, the pressure was on me too.

Recent findings suggest that I have been a copilot before, and I can tell you it’s no picnic. Rally racing in vintage cars is less about speed and more about timing. It’s an exercise that requires pinpoint accuracy at the time-stamp points in the overall course and, most critically, in the regularities. These are fiendishly short time-over-distance sections in which crossing the line just a few hundredths of a second late—or early—earns strict penalties. Sensibly, the day before the race began, Gianandrea took me out in the Aston in the Veneto countryside to practice, especially those critical regularities.

I could have opted for an easy life. The rally allowed competing cars, dating from 1931 to 1969, to use the road book or follow the course using a map in a dedicated phone app. But where’s the fun in that?

Sources indicate that “If you join a competition, you follow the regulations and strive to do your best,” Gianandrea claims. “As an Italian, if you paint numbers on the door of my car, I will want to win.”.

Industry observers note that every car in a rally like this comes with its own idiosyncrasies. On flat ground, someone driving a souped-up 2026 sports car would find these tests difficult to nail. In the reality of race conditions, the regularities often involve steep climbs or descents and unexpected corners, alling for an expert hand at the wheel—and foot on the gas pedal. The tendency of some car doors to swing open at hard bends (ours has the “suicide” doors with hinges on the back instead of the front, beloved by early carmakers) only adds to the excitement. The purpose of driver and copilot is to battle and overcome all the mechanical and computational challenges—and get our ride to the finish line bang on time.

Industry observers note that louis Vuitton has been involved in these glamorous and exacting vintage rallies since 1993. The Dolomites Run represents an enthusiastic return to the genre after a fourteen-year gap and, perhaps tellingly, the company’s global sponsorship (since 2025) of Formula 1. Unconfirmed rumors circulated in the field that the choice of ending the rally at a Grand Prix could well be repeated—and soon—in other countries in the future.

It’s easy, after all, to see why a fusion of style and cars with six- and seven-figure price tags might appeal to Louis Vuitton and competitors alike. Not surprisingly, at every coffee and lunch stop, the LV effect sprinkled the race with an added sense of luxury. In between, our snaking caravan carried the glamour of a century of motoring along with it. At every hairpin you got a glimpse of a gull-wing Mercedes, a 1931 Bugatti two-seater (my personal fave), and a shimmering behemoth of a Bentley in quick succession. These cars would turn heads anywhere. But in Italy, arguably the home of the sports car, they brought smiles, applause, and gasps in even the tiniest village that passed by in our slipstream. I swear I even saw a nun with a glint in her eye at one set of traffic lights.

Navigating, I was swiftly learning, is not so much about providing a constant babble of information as it is knowing how to give clear and simple instructions—and only when strictly needed. As the finish neared in Monza at the end of two long days on the road, I was able to give Gianandrea the most helpful instruction of all: “Nothing for 15 kilometers.”.

“That,” he very kindly replied, “is the mark of a pro.”.

Even after the engines cooled, we were still clueless about how well we’d done overall. That changed at the final event, a dinner inside the Sforzesco Castle in Milan. Gianandrea stepped up, beaming, as winner of the race, and for the first time as driver. I stood somewhat sheepishly behind him as copilot as he received the trophy from Pietro Beccari, CEO of both Louis Vuitton and Louis Vuitton Fashion Group. It was an impressive swirl of Murano glass created by Venini, housed in its own equally impressive traveling case, made (naturellement) at Louis Vuitton’s atelier in Asnières.

Gianandrea has promised me visiting rights.

A Complete Timeline of the Cyrus Family Drama, From Tish and Billy Ray’s Divorce to Miley’s Wedding

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Miley Cyrus’s family has had so much drama going on over the last four years, I can only assume producers over at E! are right now trying to sign them up for a reality show. And tbh, we’d tune in. But if you haven’t been Keeping Up With the Cyruses, gather round because it’s equal parts complicated and messy.

The short version: Everyone picked sides when Tish Cyrus and Billy Ray Cyrus got divorced, but after years of feuding, it seems the family may have buried the hatchet to all come together for Miley’s wedding...for now, anyway. Baffled? Same, so let’s dive in.

Tish filed for divorce from Billy Ray in April 2022, and they released the following joint statement to People:.

I mean, sounds pretty chill! But Tish has since claimed she put up with “disrespect in every form” during the marriage, so...it seems like there was more going on behind the scenes than fans initially thought.

In fact, just a few months after Tish and Billy’s split announcement, a source told E! News that “the divorce between her parents has put a strain on [Miley’s] relationship with her dad and it’s been hard to connect with him in the last year. She hopes they can eventually work on their relationship.”.

Tish married Prison Break star Dominic Purcell in August 2023, and the internet was quick to clock that neither Noah Cyrus nor Braison Cyrus were in the bridal party (whereas Miley Cyrus, Brandi Cyrus, and Trace Cyrus were).

Instead, Noah and Braison seemingly spent the day chilling at Walmart and posted a selfie that featured Noah in a Billy Ray Cyrus t-shirt.

A few months after, a source confirmed to Us Weekly that Noah has “always been close with Billy Ray,” adding that this has also “caused a rift between her and Miley.”.

Oh, and another insider claimed, “The family dynamics haven’t been the same since the divorce, and now that Tish and Billy Ray are with other people, there’s even more division among them all.”.

While Miley and her sister have historically been close, fans spotted the first signs of drama in October 2023, when Noah wrote, “The disrespect in this video...” in the comment section of a clip of Miley on The Joe Rogan Experience.

Right around the same time, Billy Ray married Firerose—but it’s unclear whether any of Billy’s children were in attendance.

After winning an award at the 2024 Grammys, Miley left Billy out of her acceptance speech, and a source later told Us Weekly that he’d been attempting to reach out with congratulations.

Recent findings suggest that “He’s tried reaching out to Miley many times and congratulated her on her Grammys,” the insider remarked. “The kids have chosen sides, but friends are hoping the rift doesn’t last forever. Miley and Billy Ray are on the outs. Miley’s very close with her mom and is standing by her.”.

Another source put it more simply, saying, “Miley hasn’t gotten over the disrespect she feels Billy Ray showed Tish and the family.”.

Later on in the month, in a truly wild plot twist, an insider alleged to Us Weekly, “Noah was [seeing] Dominic when Tish started pursuing him,” adding Tish “was aware" of the situation and that “the turmoil between Noah and Tish goes far beyond [what people think]. Noah is very distraught over Tish stealing Dominic from her.”.

Important note: Tish later claimed that she and Dominic met via DMs and did not mention anything about Noah...

Us Weekly also spoke to a source who remarked, “Noah and Tish haven’t spoken since the whole thing happened with Dominic,” and that “Tish is spiraling out of control and trying to figure out how to defuse this.” According to this person, Noah and Dominic were dating for “about eight to nine months” but were “having challenges.”.

However! The Daily Mail spoke to an anonymous insider who claimed, “Noah never dated Dominic and they were not together. She is delusional to think otherwise and is trying to create a narrative that will paint her as a victim.” This source emphasized that “Noah was not invited to Tish’s wedding and she would not have come even if she was. Tish wanted a peaceful wedding and did not want Noah to create any sort of scene.”.

In a recent development, the insider went on to add, “Noah has always craved the attention because she did not get it growing up. Tish was always so Miley-sided because that is where the money was. Miley and Tish are like sisters and Noah has always been envious of this because she’s never had a connection with Tish like Miley has.”.

Recent findings suggest that when it comes to whether or not Miley knew about Noah and Dominic, sources differ. One person told People, “Miley had no idea about the drama with Dominic” and “confronted her mom about it,” while another told Us Weekly that Miley “absolutely knew” and was “fully aware.” Yikes!!!!

Yep! The musician shared a birthday message on Instagram for her mom in May amid the duo’s alleged feud alongside the caption, “Happy Birthday Mom.”.

Aaaaaaand by July, the two were seen out and about together in Los Angeles.

During her My Next Guest Needs No Introduction episode, which aired in June, Miley explained (per E!), “Honestly, my mom is my hero. My father—I’m grateful for being able to watch him ahead of me. He’s almost given me this map. There is a map of what to do and what not to do. And he’s guided me on both.”.

Industry observers note that she continued, “My dad had a really rough childhood. And my childhood—I mean, we can go and talk about the hard times or the struggles—but I had food, I had love, I grew up in a beautiful substantial house and my dad didn’t have that.”.

Miley’s rare comments were aired amid Billy Ray filing for divorce from Firerose after seven months of marriage due to irreconcilable differences and “inappropriate marital conduct.”.

It has been revealed that following his dad’s performance at Trump’s inauguration Liberty Ball, Trace posted an open letter to Billy on Instagram, expressing concern for his health. Trace noted, “Me and the girls have been genuinely worried about you for years but you’ve pushed all of us away.”.

In a recent development, he went on to add, “Noah desperately has wanted you to be a part of her life and you haven’t even been there for her. That’s your baby girl. She deserves better. Somehow just like me she still idolizes you though.”.

Apparently, Billy Ray later threatened him with “legal action” for his public plea, because three days later, Trace followed up with since-deleted IG note, explaining that his open letter “was beyond loving” and that he “could have been extremely honest about a lot more.”.

Billy ended up making a cryptic statement, saying, “Giving thanks for the California Rain . Praying for the brokenhearted and their pain. Praying for my family. For my children … sons and daughters…and their mother. Let this moment be the start of healing ❤️‍🩹 for us all. ‘The past does not equal the future.’ Amen.”.

After Trace’s open letter to Billy Ray went viral, Braison (who helped Billy produce his latest album) took to his IG Stories to respond to his older bro, noting that their dad was “happy, healthy, and ready to make this record.”.

A fan then slid into Trace’s DMs to question Braison’s post, and Trace replied with this cryptic message: “Birds of a feather flock together.” Well then!

Meanwhile, a “Cyrus family source” told People that family was attempting to work things out. “They got through the drama of 2024, and it’s a newly introduced year,” the source noted. “Miley and Noah and Braison and Tish, they don’t want to be this Cyrus family feud. This is not enjoyable for them.”.

Per a source for People, “Miley used to feel overwhelmed by the family drama. She worked hard to remove herself. She’s not about to get involved again. She’s in a great place now. She’s thriving and looking out for herself.”.

For Braison’s 31st birthday, Miley and her fiancé Maxx Morando joined Billy on his farm in Tennessee, and her dad snapped a cute selfie to prove it.

Sources indicate that during a profile with The Latest York Times that same month, Miley revealed that she and Billy have healed their bond. “As I’ve gotten older, I’m respecting my parents as individuals instead of as parents—because my mom really loved my dad for her whole life, and I think being married to someone in the music industry and not being a part of it is obviously really hard,” Miley stated at the time. “And so I think I took on some of my mom’s hurt as my own because it hurt her more than it hurt me as an adult, and so I owned a lot of her pain.”.

She added, “But now that my mom is so in love with my stepdad, who I completely adore, and now that my dad, I see him finding happiness, too—I can love them both as individuals instead of as a parental pairing.”.

The following month, during an interview on Monica Lewinsky’s podcast, Miley opened up about “Secrets” off the deluxe edition of her album Something Beautiful.

“I wrote this song about my dad, because I wanted him to tell me even though there were secrets, even though I didn't really want to know,” she explained. “I wanted to be the one he felt safe enough to tell me the things that were damning and damaging to the family. I wanted him to think that as a middle child, I’m old enough that I could take some of that.”.

She also talked about where her family stood in general, saying, “My family and I have had a really difficult…What did you call your decade? Dark decade. Yeah, we had one of those.”.

She continued, “Half of us weren't speaking to each other at one point, and we cleaned all that up. That was a really important part of my year this year, was all of my family putting those lines of communication back together. A lot because of, you know, I had a lot of loyalty to my mom, the way that families do when parents get divorced.”.

Miley sat down with her mom and sisters for an interview with The Cut, where it was revealed that the Cyrus ladies are all on good terms.

At one point, Miley stated, “One thing I’ve always loved about our family is that we’re very honorable and respectful of each other’s differences; I think a lot of families get torn apart from their differences...but as we’ve gotten older, we’ve found our own opinions and ideas individually.”.

To celebrate 20 years of Hannah Montana, Miley starred in a TV special, during which both of her parents made appearances.

Miley tied the knot with Maxx in Palm Springs, where—according to a source for People—“the most special part was seeing Miley’s family all come together to celebrate her.”.

In attendance were Miley’s parents Tish and Billy, Billy’s girlfriend Elizabeth Hurley and her son Damian Hurley, Tish’s husband Dominic, Miley’s sister Noah and her fiancé Pinkus, and Miley’s sister Brandi and her fiancé Matt Southcombe.

It’s unclear, however, whether Miley’s brothers Trace and Braison (or her half-brother Christopher Cody) were there.

Does Anyone Care How Yellowjackets Ends Anymore?

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, believe it or not, Yellowjackets is based on real events.
  • According to recent reports, yellowjackets, in a way, explores what might have happened had the group never revealed just how they managed to survive in the wilderness.
  • The series explored survival in all its forms, from the lasting effects of grief to the need for women to escape their mundane, suburban lives for a little danger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, believe it or not, Yellowjackets is based on real events. In 1972, a high school rugby team, along with their families, boarded Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571 and crashed in the Andes. Only sixteen of the forty-five passengers survived when they were rescued seventy-two days later, and they all harbored a dark secret: To survive, they ate the flesh of the people who had died.

According to recent reports, yellowjackets, in a way, explores what might have happened had the group never revealed just how they managed to survive in the wilderness. Much like Uruguayan Air Force Flight 571, the Showtime series follows a high school women’s soccer team that survives a plane crash by killing and eating each other. Cocreators Ashley Lyle and Bart Nickerson blended in potential supernatural elements such as a dark presence that possibly forces them to kill, classic Lord of the Flies homages, and a killer soundtrack. Yellowjackets also cut ahead to each survivor’s life as an adult, featuring the acting talents of Melanie Lynskey, Christina Ricci, and Juliette Lewis. For a while, it was engrossing TV.

The series explored survival in all its forms, from the lasting effects of grief to the need for women to escape their mundane, suburban lives for a little danger. It was critically acclaimed, nominated for awards, and topped many “Best of the Year” lists. But then, five years and two more chaotic seasons went by that really seemed to test its audience’s … well, appetites.

Now that the fourth and final season is upon us—season 4 premiered on Friday, November 20—the answers to Yellowjackets’ burning questions will finally be revealed. Namely: Is something forcing them to kill each other, or can everything be explained by science? Will the public find out that they resorted to ritualistic murder and cannibalism? And, most importantly, is there anyone left who’s still interested in finding out?

To be fair, there’s already something of an answer to that last question. Despite critical fatigue for the series, over two million viewers tuned in to the season 3 premiere last year, per Paramount. That number then increased a bit to 3 million by the season 3 finale. Sure, those numbers pale in comparison to The Pitt season 2’s 15.4 million average weekly viewers or even the Landman season 2 premiere’s 9.2 million viewers. But there is a fan base willing to see this series to the end, whatever happens.

Recent findings suggest that what is that ending? Where the series presently stands, our girls are finally returning home after being rescued. They’ll likely adjust to normal life again by committing another hunt back in their hometown. And in the present, the promise of “last one standing” in the pre-roll recap likely points to a final bloodbath. Is that even what fans want? Until that finale, how everything will resolve, and what it all really means, remains a mystery.

For the Uruguayans, they faced a moral and religious crisis when they returned. When news broke that the rugby team ate the flesh of their dead passengers, one of the survivors defended their actions by comparing it to that of Jesus Christ and the Eucharist. According to the survivor, the group made a pact to sacrifice their bodies for each other if they perished so that they could eat their flesh to survive. The media circus completely flipped, and they were heroes once again. Pope Paul VI even wrote them a letter to sanctify their actions. It’s a fascinating end to their story—but one that the Yellowjackets cocreators likely found made for an entirely different sort of TV show.

It has been revealed that outside of the pagan imagery and supernatural threats that the Yellowjackets cast face, religion has yet to enter the picture. The cannibalism mostly seemed inevitable until it finally happened halfway through season 2, and besides that, the women have done much worse since returning home. After three seasons of one cold-blooded murder after another, the body count just to keep their secret hidden is enough for all of them to face the electric chair. And even if there is a malevolent force controlling them, it may take a metaphorical release of pain and grief on par with Hereditary or Weapons to fully satisfy viewers in the series finale.

“To some extent, I do feel as though if we were to just 100 percent jump both feet on one side of [the supernatural/reality] line, it would disperse some of what makes this show interesting,” cocreator Ashley Lyle told CBR ahead of season 4.

It has been revealed that “I think that we are fully aware that we are either going to delight or anger both sides of that equation in some way, shape, or form,” they added. “But I don’t know that that could have been avoided.”.

It has been revealed that at this point, some version of watching the women all kill each other, or even watching them all defeat the evil they believe is haunting them, just doesn’t feel like enough. The show’s biggest problem might have just been that it ran too long. A simpler ending to a shorter story might have left viewers delighted. But we shall see! If Yellowjackets can land the plane (sorry) in the end, I’m willing to eat (apologies again) my own words on this one.

Azzedine Alaïa Changed Fashion on His Own Terms

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the 1980s, Azzedine Alaïa acquired a title that followed him for the rest of his career: the “King of Cling.” The moniker was a fitting one: the Tunisian couturier was renowned for his sculptural, body-centric designs. He experimented with stretch jersey and “anti-stress” fibers to sculpt the body without restricting movement.

But the nickname was also limiting, failing to capture the full scope of his work. The first major U.S. retrospective devoted to Alaïa, “Azzedine Alaïa: Sculpting Fashion,” at San Francisco’s Legion of Honor, brings his broader legacy into focus through 80 garments and selections from his personal collection of historic fashion.

Recent findings suggest that “As my research went on, I came to realize how important the U.S. market was in Alaïa’s launch,” Laura L. Camerlengo, co-curator of the exhibit and curator in charge of Costume and Textile Arts at the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco, tells ELLE. “By the [brand’s] third season, the U.S. was the second highest market after France, [with interest from] both luxury department stores and small independent retailers.”.

The exhibition took shape after Camerlengo reached out to Olivier Saillard, director of the Fondation Azzedine Alaïa in Paris, who became her co-curator. As visitors enter the Legion of Honor’s Rosekrans Court, they encounter a dress designed for Grace Jones: a spring/summer 1986 haute couture look that Jones modeled on the runway and wore to the 1985 Oscars de la Mode. Part of the opening display, titled “The Women Who Made Alaïa,” it sets the tone for a show that recognizes the muses—both famous and private clients—who wore and supported his work.

Also on view are looks made famous by Rihanna—namely, a sheer red halter gown with a flowing train that she wore to the 2013 Grammys—and Tina Turner, whose silk-organza dress embroidered with gold-tone beads from Alaïa’s spring/summer 1989 concludes the exhibition.

The show then turns to Alaïa’s iconography, as Camerlengo puts it: the bandage dress, his work in denim, and zippered dresses, as well as rare, lesser-seen gems. “I was really keen to have early works on view, particularly the pieces from the 1980s, when he was launching his brand,” the curator claims. “These are pieces that would have been shown at Bergdorf Goodman when he had his first fashion show in the United States.”.

According to recent reports, the exhibition also places Alaïa’s designs in conversation with the museum’s permanent collection. Belle Epoque-style ensembles from his spring/summer 1992 collection appear among 18th-century European paintings and furnishings, including a Canaletto view of Venice and a sofa commissioned for Marie Antoinette.

Alaïa’s own collection of historic fashion, previously shown in the 2023 Paris exhibition “Azzedine Alaïa, couturier collectionneur,” is represented here, too. The gallery includes pieces by fashion houses he admired, such as Lanvin, Chanel, Balenciaga, and Schiaparelli.

Sources indicate that though Alaïa, who died in 2017 at age 82, is remembered for the body-conscious designs that earned him that “King of Cling” title, he was also a renegade in an industry built around constant production. He showed collections only when he felt they were ready—a maverick approach that still resonates today—and had his creations worn by a who’s who of the modeling world, from Naomi Campbell to Gisele Bündchen. Many of his designs were featured in the pages of ELLE over the decades.

In a recent development, “He was someone who pioneered a new way of thinking about fashion,” Camerlengo notes. “He was one of the first to question the fashion system and seasonal calendars and the need for trends. He was focused on meticulous craftsmanship and intentionality in design, a sort of precedent to what we think about today, where we are critical of overproduction and overconsumption in fashion.”.

According to recent reports, “Azzedine Alaïa: Sculpting Fashion” is on view at the Legion of Honor Museum from Nov. 21, 2026, to Apr. 11, 2027.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

According to recent reports, walk, don’t run, your next nail appointment... OPI has cracked open its polish vault, and some of the best, previously retired OPI nail polish colors have officially made their comeback. In honor of its 45th anniversary, the brand has brought back about a dozen iconic shades that mani lovers have been begging to see again, plus even more shades inspired by OGs for a grand total of 24 new(ish) polishes.

It has been revealed that meet OPI’s Most Requested Collection, which combines several previously-retired fan favorites with some fresh shades inspired by some of the brand’s most beloved colors. The collection includes everything from vampy Lincoln Park at Midnight and nostalgic pink Mod About You Pastel to Route Beer Float, a very ‘90s, shimmery mauve. This fall 2026 collection includes 24 permanent shades, meaning these colors aren’t just making a brief cameo before disappearing again—they’re back for good. Twelve of them are offered in the classic OPI Nail Lacquer formula, while the other 12 have come back in the longer-lasting Infinite Shine option.

Whether you’re excited to reunite with an old favorite, discover a cult classic you missed the first time around, or try a new shade inspired by some of these icons, I highly recommend giving the full collection a scroll. To get you started, here are 12 shades from this buzzy launch that I’m especially excited to try.

She’s baaaaccckkkkk! The inky purple shade originally introduced exactly 20 years ago and is the shimmery sister to one of my all-time faves, Lincoln Park After Dark. You know those polishes that look black until the light hits them? That’s exactly what you’re getting with this ultra moody, ultra iconic shade.

In a recent development, another shade straight from the vault, this 2012 rich, deep violet with red shimmer became an instant favorite when it originally debuted. If you love burgundy nails for the colder months, consider your next manicure handled.

It may be fall, but not every manicure needs to be dark and moody rn. Mod About You Pastel polish brings a soft, creamy pink into the mix, making it a pretty option for anyone who prefers a sweet, minimalist manicure over the season’s deeper shades. It’s a slightly warmer-toned sister to another one of my faves, Mod About You.

Originally released in 1997, Route Beer Float is the oldest shade OPI brought back for this collection. A mauve-meets-caramel shimmery shade makes it a particularly chic option for the chocolate brown and chai latte manicures that have been everywhere this season.

Quiet luxury nail lovers, this one’s for you. Berlin There, Doin’ That is a creamy, light taupe that puts a fresh spin on OPI’s beloved Berlin There, Done That shade. It’s a little lighter and softer than the original, with a greige-like finish that makes it the perfect understated neutral.

OPI Ink fans, rejoice! Your favorite deep violet is getting a second life with Don’t Over Ink It. The shimmery, deep, inky navy-purple has all the moody, mysterious appeal of the original, but this latest version is shimmery rather than sparkly and leans a little more navy. Overall, though, the two are pretty dang similar. Is this your sign to revisit your purple polish era? I think yes.

Say bonjour to your next favorite neutral. This chic, creamy mauve-ish nude pays homage to the beloved Tickle My France-y shade. It’s more of a neutral than its predecessor, which was a much rosier, dusty-rose-meets-mauve shade. It’s soft, sophisticated, and gives your nails that effortlessly polished, je ne sais quoi look. Oui oui!

Industry observers note that did ya miss her? Talk about a throwback... It’s All Greek to Me is back from the archives, bringing its vivid, shimmery fuchsia pink finish along for the ride. The bold, metallic shade makes a statement, so I can see why OPI fans begged for its return. I’m ready to paint a couple coats on my fingertips ahead of the holiday party season. Who indicates bright pink nails are just for summer?

Industry observers note that I do! I do say yes to Suzi Takes a Vow. It’s a soft, romantic peachy pink that’s giving major bridal mani energy. Wedding bells or not, consider this your sign to commit to this classic light neutral.

Industry observers note that you know when you just have to try something based on the name alone? That’s how I feel about this one. With a name like Vampire State Building, you already know this is going to be dramatic. The deep burgundy shade—originally released in 2000—delivers all the vampy energy you could want from a dark red manicure.

According to recent reports, A lot of the polishes in this latest collection are pretty opaque, but this sheer beauty is perfect for a naked nail or soap manicure moment. It’s a soft, pale pink with a barely-there finish that’s tailor-made for the clean girl mani crowd. Think your-nails-but-better, with a little extra wink. See what I did there?

It has been revealed that A classic red manicure never goes out of style, and neither does Vodka & Caviar (the nail polish or the food-and-drink combo). The expensive-looking shade is luxury in a bottle. This vibrant apple red looks just as good with jeans and a white tee as it does with your favorite holiday party outfit. Love some versatility!

Rep. Ken Calvert wins all-Republican race in California

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that california Rep.
  • Young Kim in a redrawn Southern California district that pitted the two Republicans against one another.
  • Calvert was leading his rival by 7 points Monday night when The Associated Press called the race for California’s 40th District with more than 70 percent of the vote in.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that california Rep. Ken Calvert walks down the House steps after votes on Sept. 3. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

According to recent reports, rep. Ken Calvert defeated Rep. Young Kim in a redrawn Southern California district that pitted the two Republicans against one another.

Calvert was leading his rival by 7 points Monday night when The Associated Press called the race for California’s 40th District with more than 70 percent of the vote in.

Calvert, who chairs the powerful House Defense Appropriations Subcommittee, is the longest-serving Republican in the California delegation, first winning election to Congress in 1992.

Industry observers note that the race was reshaped by the Golden State’s upcoming voter-approved House map, drawn by state Democrats in response to mid-decade redistricting by Texas Republicans. The new map dismantled Calvert’s 41st District in Riverside County, transforming it into a safely blue Democratic seat in the Los Angeles area. That prompted him to run for the redrawn 40th District, which included a sizable percentage of his current constituents.

The rare intraparty general election was possible because Calvert and Kim finished in the top two slots in the state’s June primary. Under the California system, all candidates run on the same primary ballot, with the top two vote-getters, regardless of party, advancing to November.

Calvert had already declared victory last week, saying on social media that there was “no greater honor than serving my neighbors and our communities in Congress.”.

Kim’s defeat is the second of her congressional career — she lost her initial bid during the 2018 blue wave before winning election to the House two years later.

Industry observers note that in her concession message, Kim singled out California Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom, who led the redistricting effort last year that targeted five Republican-held districts. Democrats flipped all five seats last week.

“It’s unfortunate that Gavin Newsom’s political redistricting scheme forced two Republican members from Congress into this race,’’ she stated in a statement.

The race between was marked by rancor, with Calvert alleging that Kim was not a true conservative and supported higher taxes. Kim accused Calvert of growing rich off stock trades over his decades in Washington.

Calvert will serve in a delegation with a dramatically smaller GOP presence next year, with Democrats likely to hold 48 of California’s 52 House seats. Just two other California Republicans – Reps. Vince Fong and Tom McClintock – have been reelected so far, while a third, Rep. Jay Obernolte, narrowly leads his Democratic challenger in an as-yet-uncalled race.

The Calvert-Kim battle was not the only all-party November clash in California, with several districts featuring matchups between two Democrats.

One incumbent has already been unseated, with Rep. Jimmy Gomez losing to fellow Democrat Angela Gonzales-Torres in the Los Angeles-area 34th District, according to The Associated Press.

According to recent reports, two other blue-on-blue contests in Northern California remained uncalled as of Tuesday afternoon: Rep. Mike Thompson was trailing venture capitalist Eric Jones in the 4th District, while Rep. Doris Matsui led Sacramento City Councilmember Mai Vang in the 7th District.

15 Best Beard Oils for Taming Your Stubborn Facial Hair

📅 08 Dec 2016 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3607 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Growing a beard was only the beginning: Now you’ve gotta give it some love.
  • Recent findings suggest that I’d go so far as to rank beard oil as the second most vital beard care product, just after beard trimmers.
  • Recent findings suggest that for the longest time, I thought of Honest Amish as “that Amazon beard oil,” given its enormous popularity on the e-tailer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So, you've realized. Growing a beard was only the beginning: Now you’ve gotta give it some love. Thankfully, the best beard oil will keep that sculpted scruff feeling great! And not just for you, either, because the right beard oil leaves your skin glowing—and stops your facial hair from annoying any partner who gets close to it. Great beard oils also keep coarse hair from getting brittle and wiry, and soften your beard so you’re not scratching your neck or dealing with beard dandruff (yes, it exists). All that from just a couple drops of wonder oil.

Recent findings suggest that I’d go so far as to rank beard oil as the second most vital beard care product, just after beard trimmers. And it’s a close second. Because whether you keep your facial hair at a precise 24-hour stubble, go full hermit-mode, or stay somewhere in between, a beard oil does irreplaceable work. (The kind you can’t replace with any old moisturizer or conditioner.) So, if you’re tired of flyaways, coarse beard hair, dandruff, or itchiness, these GQ-tested and approved beard oils will turn your scruff into fluff. Promise.

Recent findings suggest that for the longest time, I thought of Honest Amish as “that Amazon beard oil,” given its enormous popularity on the e-tailer. (At the time of writing, we’re talking nearly 30,000 reviews and a 4.5-star rating.) And often, I'll intentionally seek out an alternative to these Amazon-beloved grooming products—if only because it feels like the equivalent of recommending Applebee's to an out-of-towner. But this time, well: Welcome to Applebee's.

Sources indicate that frankly, I couldn't find a better beard oil. Not only is Honest Amish cost-effective (at the second-best price-per-ounce on my list), but the brand nailed the blend. It's a pure oil recipe (no non-oil ingredients), with seven carrier oils and seven essential oils that give it an earthy scent and help tone the skin beneath your bushel. It absorbs fast, works great to smooth down flyaways, relax stiff bristles, and battle both dry skin and flake-prone beards. And did I mention the value? Six bucks per ounce is a steal.

To be clear, I only use Honest Amish on my beard, largely because I'm not a fan of using any essential oils on bare skin—I particularly find that pumpkin seed oil (a key ingredient here) can be slightly pore-clogging on acne-prone skin. That said: I count myself as acne-prone and haven't had complications with Honest Amish, so I'm probably being over-cautious. It's really just that good.

Despite the name Beardbrand, this company's product line covers the whole body, with a focus on multi-tasking grooming products like dual washes, all-purpose balms, and this utilitarian oil. You'll catch me using it on my hands, elbows, and hair—whether for a dash of shine (to offset a matte hair product) or a protective coat against frizz and humidity. But Beardbrand's Utility Oil is on this list because it works beautifully in the beard.

Industry observers note that sure, it's a touch heavier than some other oils—but that also makes it a terrific pre-shave lubricant. It's crucial to note that no matter which “flavor” you choose, this oil has a strong dash of fragrance. They're all good, but I'm partial to the brand's fresh Bold Fortune scent, which oozes a sexy combo of leather, oud, and tobacco. (And pro-tip: The brand's utility wash has the same come-hither scent, if you want to double down.).

Horace's beard oil will make a lot of you happy, though for different reasons. For those overwhelmed by scents—particularly artificial ones—you'll appreciate that its got the subtlest of aromas. I'm partial to the Lemon & Mint one, which reads as “fresh" and never overwhelms. For those looking to stay away from chemicals, Horace's formula is 99% natural—and the 1% is a synthetic grapeseed oil, not something with 12 syllables, which I'm fine with.

The brand gets bonus marks for its easily-understood ingredients labels, which break down these details and err on the side of much-appreciated transparency. Finally, if you're on the fence about beard oils, Horace will make you a believer. It absorbs fast, gives a pinch of shine, and makes just enough difference in terms of taming, moisturizing, and softening that you'll see why a beard oil makes sense.

In the grooming world, Jack Black (the brand) has earned its own fanbase, thanks in large part to one product—the signature Jack Black beard oil. Apply just a few drops and it immediately goes to work softening coarse and brittle facial hair, and without an overpowering fragrance that will distract you all day long. It's one of the most popular beard oils on Amazon, but don't hold that against it. While it softens and adds shine, this oil also delivers a dose of antioxidants and vitamins from natural ingredients such as brown algae and rosemary.

Industry observers note that it also uses a unique blend of oils with the subtlest whiff of melon fragrance. Instead of the usual suspects (jojoba, avocado, sunflower seed), this product uses Kalahari melon oil, marula oil, and plum oil, which moisturize your facial hair and skin on contact. Because these oils are all fast-absorbing (my beard hair soaks it up like a sponge), they make this product much less greasy than other beard oils, giving it a more premium feel.

I test literally hundreds of grooming products a year, and I'm so intimately acquainted with brands latest and old that I often think about them based on their best product. For Pura d'Or, it's this organic beard oil. It's the best value on this list, at $3 per fluid ounce. Given how quickly you can go through beard oil—just think, if you're applying up to twice a day, that dollar-per-ounce math becomes important. So, in addition to being my budget pick, this also gets my recommendation as the best beard oil for big beards.

Industry observers note that of course, it's only important if the formula measures up—and here, it does. There are two carrier oils, argan and jojoba, along with a bit of grapefruit peel and some sandalwood essential oil for both a natural scent and a touch of antimicrobial powers. It's a great beard oil for anyone, no matter how substantial your bank account, but if you're bearding on a budget, you'll appreciate how much goodness Pura d'Or packs into a few bucks.

Blind Barber's tonka-tinged oil is wonderful for the guy who wants to moisturize skin and whiskers with the same product. It wears extremely light—so much so that my oily skin barely registers its presence—and I find its carrier-oil-centric and shea-butter-forward formula especially comforting on the skin. It should be noted that this formula includes artificial perfume, so fragrance-averse individuals should steer clear. But for those of us who want a special scent, a flake-free beard, and soothed skin, Blind Barber's beard oil does it all.

While I'd use most of the above options as both a hair oil and a beard oil, Aesop's is one where I think of it as a hair oil first and foremost. It brings control without making things look greasy, while trapping moisture and stopping frizz. I'll use it in short hair to tame down the sides, in medium lengths (mixed with a cream or clay) for added shine, or in long hair to prevent split ends. Then, once my hair's settled up, I'll run my hands through my beard afterward. So, if you want a great hair oil with beard benefits, Aesop's is the winner.

Since the beginning of the men's grooming boom, I've been waiting for the major designer fashion houses to start catering to guys with facial hair. For now, Tom Ford's beard oil stands alone. So, how does the designer oil stack up against our everyday favorites? After trying it out, I can tell you it’s better as a fragrance than a beard oil, but the scent alone earns it a spot in this guide.

In a recent development, the tobacco vanilla fragrance is much more sophisticated than what we’re used to seeing, or smelling, in this space. The scent puts an emphasis on vanilla, and you just need one or two pumps for full coverage. Considering the price and the name on the bottle, we were shocked to find this oil comes in a plastic pump bottle, but that fragrance. If you want to buy beard oil as a gift, this premium conditioning oil is a step up over your average Amazon brand, even if it doesn't soften coarse hair as well as some of our other options.

If you have sensitive skin—or if you're afraid of your beard oil clashing with your daily cologne—then Marlowe makes one of the only fragrance-free beard oils. Most beard oil formulas contain both essential oils and some type of perfume oil (or, parfum, for my fellow ingredients detectives), which can be risky for your skin, follicles, and pores, so it’s nice to have an option for acne-prone and sensitive skin types.

According to recent reports, this beard oil couldn’t be simpler—and I mean that in a good way. Marlowe No. 143 has an all-oil formula and just four ingredients: safflower seed oil, sunflower seed oil, corn oil, and soybean oil. That’s it. Considering the average beauty product contains up to a dozen ingredients we can’t even pronounce, it’s a refreshing change. Although, I have to say, if you want the softest possible beard, Honest Amish also makes a fragrance-free oil.

In a recent development, most guys use beard oil to tame flyaways. But what if you want the thickest, fullest beard possible? In that case, I’d recommend reaching for Bevel’s oil. This brand makes skin and hair products for Black men, but anyone with coarse or curly hair can benefit from their products. GQ contributor Timothy Beck Werth reports that this oil gave him a thicker-looking beard without excess frizz, which isn't easy to do. (BTW, that’s as much as you can expect from any beard oil, so please don’t fall for the “beard growth serums” you’ll find all over the internet.).

Sources indicate that for parched facial hair, the grapeseed, macadamia, jojoba, and argan oil will condition your beard and add a healthy shine. For beneath the scruff, the avocado and primrose oil with soothe your skin without clogging up your pores and follicles. Werth indicates this beard oil instantly softened his facial hair, and he also liked the sweeter smell of the macadamia-based formula. Most beard oils opt for woodsy fragrances, and the more subtle scent profile here is a nice surprise, he explains.

Recent findings suggest that anthony’s conditioning beard oil is a 2-in-1 product—a pre-shave oil and regular beard oil. That approach can be risky, since a lot of multipurpose products try to be everything and succeed at nothing, but luckily that’s not the case here. If you regularly cycle between clean-shaven, stubble, and full-on lighthouse keeper, then you can still use this product daily. As a pre-shave oil, it moisturizes the skin and softens facial hair for a smoother shave with fewer morning-after red bumps. As a beard oil, it hydrates, then locks in that moisture so your beard stays soft and shiny all day. I found the consistency to be somewhere in between a leave-in conditioner gel and a traditional oil, making it thicker and less messy to apply.

Industry observers note that the oil also has an herbaceous, minty fragrance that’s so refreshing it feels like aromatherapy every time you run it through your hair. That’s because the formula is full of ingredients that smell good, feel good, and actually help your skin and hair. It uses carrier oils like soybean and castor to deliver skin-pleasing and antimicrobial botanicals such as rosemary, basil, tea tree oil, eucalyptus, and spearmint. And on the hydration front, calendula and olive oil nourish your whiskers into their softest, fluffiest selves. Because of the more complex fragrance and ingredients profile, this wouldn’t be my pick for guys with sensitive skin. Still, it’s a multi-functional serum you’ll look forward to using every day.

Lots of beard oils promise to get flyaways under control, yet those rogue hairs keep popping up. So, what do you do? Instead of trying yet another oil, try reaching for a product that’s more of a leave-in conditioner for your beard. We’ve previously praised Zeus’s beard brushes, but the California-based brand also makes a beard serum that deserves a spot in your bathroom cabinet. I love that this beard oil has the simplest possible ingredients list: sweet almond oil, soybean oil, argan seed oil, trihydroxystearin, avocado oil, and fragrance.

Sources indicate that the only multi-syllable ingredient there is a simple thickening agent, which gives this refined beard oil a gel-like consistency. That thicker formula will also put flyaways in their place. The very subtle fragrance is more Mediterranean than winter pine forest (we tested the Verbena Lime version), but you can also opt for a fragrance-free formula if you have sensitive skin or allergies. The plastic bottle uses an air pump, letting you get every last drop of oil. For clean freaks who hate the messiness and spillage that always comes with beard oil application, this is another bonus.

Tired of being left out of couple’s skincare night just because those stupid sheet masks won’t hold onto your glorious beard? Cardon’s got you, boo. Actually, this bead oil hack is perfect for guys who only sparingly use beard oil on an as-needed basis.

The bamboo and charcoal sheet mask is specially shaped for guys with beards, and each mask comes with a dose of beard oil made with argan and jojoba oil. In the Venn diagram of Korean skincare and beard care products, this sheet mask-beard oil duo is the tiny, microscopic bit of overlap in the middle.

The best best oil should support your skin and your beard, and Baxter of California's sweet-smelling oil doesn't sacrifice one for the other. In his guide to the best beard care products, GQ's Timothy Beck Werth stated that “In our testing, no beard oil absorbs as swiftly or spreads as evenly as this one.” Squalane helps nourish the most overlooked skin on your face, while avocado oil, vitamin E, and botanical extracts smooth out your beard.

Industry observers note that as with anything you put on your skin, the ingredients are what matter most. And with beard oils, there are two categories of ingredients: carrier oils and essential oils. No two ingredients will perform exactly the same. Some will help with very specific situations or conditions; some may actively aggravate your skin. Essential oils in particular can aggravate skin if used by themselves. So, consider the following carrier oils and essential oils, favored both by myself and Alyssa Bachowski, a senior barber at Fellow Barber’s Williamsburg, NYC barbershop.

Carrier oils—often vegetable and see oils—make up the bulk of these beard oil formulas, bringing beard nourishment and skin hydration. The most popular carrier oils are argan oil and jojoba oil (both of which Bachowski recommends), though there are dozens of varieties, from castor to marula to grape seed oils. They're usually unscented, though some—like coconut oil—may carry an aroma. Because carrier oils make up the “base” of the oil, they should be among the first to appear in a product's formula or list of ingredients.

In a recent development, “Jojoba oil is non-comedogenic, which means it will not clog your pores. It is also a lighter oil that is absorbent, so it won't just sit on top of the hair and give you a greasy appearance,” Bachowski notes. Along with argan oil, you’re going to see a lot of jojoba oil in most popular beard oil blends.

“Argan oil is filled with a ton of vitamins and minerals, as well as linoleic acid, sterolins, and squalene. All of these aid in protecting and keeping your skin and beard healthy,” Bachowski says.

It has been revealed that “Castor oil is known for promoting beard hair growth,” says Bachowski. It’s hypothetically the best beard-growth oil of the crew, because it acts like a vitamin for your strands—though there's more on that below in the FAQs. But don't expect it to grow more hairs, or thicker hairs. Castor oil does have a smoke-and-mirrors benefit, at least. “It is a heavier oil and dark in color, so it can give the appearance of a denser beard on men with dark facial hair,” Bachowski says.

Grape seed oil can help tone down your skin's oil production, and is extremely moisturizing for scruff and skin alike.

Rich in fatty acids, this is a frontrunner for “most nourishing oil” for your skin and whiskers.

Yes, shea butter is in fact a carrier oil, and it has supremely moisturizing properties that make it great for detangling scraggly beards and softening stiff hairs.

Sources indicate that essential oils are distillations from more potent sources, and they tend to be additive—and active—ingredients in a beard oil. These oils are typically extracted through steaming methods, and their range of benefits can include antimicrobial properties, oil-toning abilities, and soothing superpowers. Typically, any natural fragrance in a beard oil will come from essential oils. But pure essential oils can be extremely damaging to the skin.

“You should not apply pure essential oil to a beard—it will do the opposite of what you are trying to achieve,” Bachowski says. “These [pure oils] are not good for your beard nor your skin. as they can be irritating and harmful. Essential oils can cause dryness, itchiness, and redness—and some people may have allergic reactions to them.” This is exactly why you want beard oils from trusted, tested brand.

According to recent reports, bachowski likes cedarwood oil for its naturally astringent properties. “It helps cleanse the pores and prevent ingrown hairs,” she adds. It also adds a natural fragrance.

“Sandalwood has anti-inflammatory properties that help reduce any skin irritation,” Bachowski states of this deliciously scented oil.

Lavender helps calm inflammation and redness, notes Bachowski. Plus it brings lavender's soothing scent.

This antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, oil-toning ingredient is terrific for acne-prone faces and oily skin types.

Along with its refreshing scent, grapefruit peel oil helps nourish and detangle.

As GQ's lead grooming product reviewer, I've tried just about every beard oil in the biz. The ones chosen for this roundup excel at protecting and moisturizing both skin and hair, with minimal risk for things like inverse reactions and blemishes. They absorb cleanly, unless they expressly choose not to (like those which expressly use silicone), and they smell terrific (with both natural and artificially scented options). I've tested beard oils for a decade, on a beard that's been long, short, and everything in between. I've also scoured online reviews to confirm that these products are backed by throngs of loyal fans, whose collective opinion echoes my own experiences.

What is the best beard oil according to GQ?

Industry observers note that with more than a decade of testing beard oils under his belt, GQ’s expert tester chose Honest Amish as the best beard oil. And 29,000 Amazon shoppers have rated this same product 4.5 out of 5 stars.

Industry observers note that what is the difference between beard balm vs. oil?

Both beard balm and beard oil are both terrific for facial hair—but they don't do the same job. Beard balm is optimal for taming and styling facial hair, especially at medium and longer lengths. Beard oil provides less control over the shape and style, but is excellent at softening and conditioning the hairs and the skin underneath (preventing beard itch, beard dandruff, and split ends).

Recent findings suggest that after using a beard wash, most beard oils are applied the same way: “Start off with 2-3 drops in the palm of your hand,” notes Bachowski. “Rub it into your hands so that it is evenly distributed from fingertips to the heel of your hand. Start by rubbing the oil with your fingertips onto the skin beneath the beard hair, then eventually working the oil from root to tip of the actual beard. Make sure to also apply oil to your neck and cheeks where you may have shaved or trimmed as well. If you feel like the 2-3 drops wasn't enough based on the length or density of your beard, apply another 2-3 drops.”.

How do you prevent beard dandruff?

Preventing beard dandruff starts with changing your skincare regimen. Namely, introducing exfoliation and moisturizing products that can get past a thick nest of facial hair. For exfoliation, look for physical scrubs (even a beard brush will work). For the best moisturizing effects, be sure to apply beard oil both morning and night. The beard oil will also soften and condition the facial hair to prevent itchiness.

Does beard oil help grow a beard?

It has been revealed that no, beard oil is not meant to help beard hair growth, whether that’s to make facial hair thicker or grow faster. To be honest, we don’t know of much that can really change your scruff's density besides a beard transplant and maybe minoxidil. Beard oil is here to make your existing beard hair softer and more cooperative, while also nourishing the skin beneath the beard—skin that’s often prone to dehydration and dandruff. It’s already doing a lot.

Recent findings suggest that absolutely. Beard oil is a great investment for anyone with facial hair, since it can help soften and tame your scruff while simultaneously moisturizing the skin underneath. This means no more itching, no flyaways, and no beard dandruff.

Alyssa Bachowski is a senior barber at Fellow Barber’s Williamsburg NYC barbershop location.
