📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we love. Promise.

It has been revealed that as we haircare lovers all know, Dyson has truly solidified itself as the crème de la crème of buzzy hair tools. From the viral Airwrap i.d. to the OG Supersonic Hair Dryer, Dyson = high-tech hairstyling. Despite the higher price points, these tools are everywhere these days, from your favorite creator doing their hair on your TikTok feed to your hairstylist doing your hair in the salon chair. It seems like everyone loves a Dyson product (and that includes pretty much every Cosmo editor too). They’ve won tonssss of Cosmo beauty awards, including a 2025 Holy Grail Beauty Award and 2026 Reader’s Choice Beauty Award for the Airwrap, back-to-back wins in the Reader’s Choice Beauty Awards in 2024 and 2025 for the Supersonic, and many, many more.

Industry observers note that however, at $250-$500 a pop, it’s not like most people can afford to own every single Dyson tool out there. So which ones are the most worth the hundreds of dollars they cost? Luckily, we’ve here at Cosmo have tested all of ‘em—these are the ones we truly recommend spending money on.

Why we love it: Despite so many Airwrap dupes out there, us Cosmo editors keep going back to the original Dyson hair styling tool that changed the game forever. Talk about true innovation—the Airwrap created a whole upcoming category of styling products that dry, curl, volumize, straighten, and blow out hair all in one handy tool that, oh by the way, uses hot air instead of high heat that could potentially damage your hair more.

It’s also on rare sale right now—23 percent off—for Black Friday and Cyber Monday, so if you’ve been thinking of scooping one up, this is your time to shine. Run, don’t walk!

According to recent reports, one Cosmo editor notes: “If the Airwrap has zero fans, I’m dead. For years, I didn’t know how to style my hair. The round-brush-and-dryer combo was a lot for me, I didn’t know how to curl my hair, and quite honestly, all I ever did was straighten it with a flat iron (which was perfect for the mid-2010s style at the time). But when I got my hands on my first Airwrap, that all changed. Suddenly, I could do it all, and I was imparting wayyy less heat damage onto my strands than if I had been using traditional hot tools. The i.d. is great because the it has all the attachments I need, it dries and styles my thick, wavy hair super rapidly, it eliminates frizz, and keeps my style in place all day.” —CATHARINE MALZAHN, CONTRIBUTING BEAUTY WRITER.

Sources indicate that why we love it: The one that started it all and turned hair dryers from a humble styling tool into a must-have item... Dyson’s Supersonic dryer launched 10 years ago in 2016, yet it still remains one of the best hair dryers out there. And honestly, it’s not hard to see why. Beyond the basics you’d be looking for (long cord, negative ions, multiple heat and speed settings, relatively lightweight, that kind of thing), its powerful airflow dries hair noticeably quickly while the dryer monitors the temperature 40 times a second to prevent extreme heat on your strands.

It has been revealed that it’s pretty straightforward and easy to use, making a salon-worthy blowout at home feel a whole lot less intimidating. A decade later, the Supersonic is proof that some beauty investments really do stand the test of time.

One Cosmo editor indicates: “This is the first Dyson hair tool I ever used, and I still think it's probably the most worth-it tool price-wise if you wanted to splurge on one thing. I used to hate blow dryers until I tried this one. It's quick and powerful without sacrificing the health of my hair. This fully dries my hair in under two minutes (yes, two), but it doesn't leave my hair crunchy or fried either.” —BETH GILLETTE, BEAUTY EDITOR.

Why we love it: Straightening without hot plates? And you can use it on wet hair? Sign me up. The Dyson Airstrait uses airflow to dry and straighten hair at the same time, meaning you can skip the blow-dryer-and-flat-iron combo entirely. Perfect if you’re trying to cut down on styling time in the morning!

Industry observers note that unlike traditional flat irons, the Airstrait doesn’t use heated plates. Instead, it uses airflow to smooth and dry hair, delivering a soft, naturally straight finish with movement rather than that super-flat, pin-straight look. Plus, it has a dry mode for touching up your style between washes. When our editors with varying curl patterns (from wavy and fine to 4b curls) tested it, it straightened with ease and speed.

According to recent reports, one Cosmo editor notes: “I have an interesting hair type because while it’s curly and fine, I have a lot of it. It can take a very long time for me to dry my hair, but the Airstrait cut my styling time dramatically. This tool takes my hair from damp to fully dry in under 10 minutes. However, it did take a slight learning curve at first.” —MARY HONKUS, CONTRIBUTING BEAUTY WRITER.

Recent findings suggest that why we love it: Meet the Dyson hair dryer that had three Cosmo beauty editors with three different hair types completely obsessed. The Dyson Supersonic r takes everything we love about the original Supersonic and makes it lighter, smaller, and easier to maneuver, thanks to its curved, ergonomic design. In fact, it’s so lightweight that it weighs less than a pound, making it perfect for professional stylists as well as anyone who doesn’t want an arm workout just to dry hair.

Speaking of which, your arms probably won’t get super tired because of how rapidly it works. Beauty director Lauren Balsamo said it dried her soaking-wet hair in just six minutes(!!!). Add in the intelligent attachments that automatically adjust heat and airflow and remember those settings for the next time you use it, the multiple attachments, and the compact size, and it’s easy to be willing to overlook the hefty price tag.

One Cosmo editor indicates: “The first thing I noticed when I picked up the Supersonic R was the weight, or rather, the lack thereof. It seriously feels like you're holding a bottle of hairspray—that’s how airy and easy it is to handle. Then came the assembly. The magnetic attachments snapped on effortlessly. And as a wavy-haired girl who can either lean curly or reach for a round brush for a bouncy blowout, I really appreciated the range of attachments for everything from creating curls to smoothing flyaways.” —JASMINE HYMAN, ASSISTANT BEAUTY EDITOR.

Why we love it: Dyson finally made a one-step blow dryer brush, and at $250, it’s the brand’s lowest-priced hair tool (though it’s still an investment!). Like the Airwrap, the Dyson Airsmooth is another wet-to-dry styler, using powerful airflow to dry and smooth strands without extreme heat. Its teardrop shape helps you get closer to the root for more lift and volume, while the bristles are designed to minimize snagging, pulling, or breakage. It can smooth thick, wavy hair in under 15 minutes, leaving it sleek, shiny, and noticeably less frizzy.

If you’re shopping for a upcoming blow dryer brush, this is a great pick. It’s perfect for anyone who loves a smooth, bouncy blowout but doesn’t want all the bells and whistles of an Airwrap.

One Cosmo editor says: “I was thrilled to find out Dyson had created a one-stop tool for drying and styling, complete with upgraded bristle technology. I want to preserve as many of my precious strands as possible, and what I love most about this tool (besides the low-for-Dyson price) is that its bristles aren’t your basic plastic teeth that tug at your hair. Instead, they bend with your strands as you pull the brush through, releasing them rather than fighting against the tension. I usually finish styling with a solid clump of hair left behind on my tool, but with the Airsmooth, there were truly fewer than five strands caught in the bristles.” —JH.

Why we love it: An update from the iconic and original Supersonic, this even-more-high-tech dryer features a Scalp Protect mode that uses sensors to detect how close the tool is to your head and automatically adjusts the heat to help maintain a scalp temperature of approximately 131°F. Translation: You can dry your roots without blasting your scalp with so much heat that you flinch when your dryer gets too close.

It also features intelligent attachments that remember your preferred settings, plus a Pause Detect function that reduces airflow when you put the dryer down. And, of course, you still get the powerful, fast-drying performance Dyson is known for.

Industry observers note that one Cosmo editor claims: “I have the Supersonic at my parents' house (I gifted my old one to my mom a few years ago), but the Nural is at mine. This is the more high-tech version of the Supersonic, which automatically shifts air flow and heat based on how close the tool is to your scalp. If blow dryers often feel like they're burning off your scalp, this one will turn that around.” —BG.

How to choose the best Dyson hair tool.

It’s all about your hair styling goals.

Dyson hair tools are definitely not one-size-fits-all, and what works wonders on someone’s fine, straight hair might not do the same for thick curls or coils.

Recent findings suggest that before dropping hundreds of dollars on a Dyson, ask yourself: What do I actually want this thing to do? If you’re constantly switching up your hairstyle, the Airwrap’s versatility might justify the splurge. But if your goal is simply to dry your hair promptly, you probably don't need all those attachments—a Supersonic will do the trick. Love a sleek, straight finish? Try the Airstrait. Simply consider which tools you’d actually see yourself using every day before taking the plunge.

Short answer: Heck yeah! There’s a reason Dyson hair tools have earned cult-favorite status among us beauty editors, hairstylists, and pretty much everyone on TikTok. We’ve tested practically every Dyson out there, and we’re consistently impressed. For thick, long, or doesn’t-want-to-stay-styled hair, these can be especially worth the money.

According to recent reports, of course, there’s no denying that they’re a serious investment. So if you’re looking for a budget alternative, there are plenty of options out there too. But in our experience, the Dyson’s quick-drying capabilities sans excessive heat damage, customizable settings, and long-lasting results make them worth the splurge—especially if you’re someone who styles their hair regularly. And while you certainly don't need to own every Dyson tool (your bank account can thank us later), finding the right one for your hair type and styling goals can be a total game changer.

How Anthony Boyle Got Inside the Mind of Sam Bankman-Fried

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2296 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, anthony Boyle is in awe of the angels.
  • In a recent development, it’s Friday at New York Comic Con when I occupy a table for a video call with Anthony Boyle.
  • Sources indicate that soon he’ll appear in I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, about tight-knit friends with unfulfilled dreams in the UK, which drew rave reviews at Cannes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, anthony Boyle is in awe of the angels. “This is so good,” he says as a boyish smile forms on his 32-year-old face. Dressed in an immaculate black-and-pale-gold track jacket and pinstripe slacks, Boyle points through the Zoom screen, asking who the characters behind me are. I confess I don’t know. But the pair of fire-orange cosplay wings in my peripheral are hard to miss. “You gotta keep all this in,” Boyle says. (This is me upholding a promise.).

In a recent development, it’s Friday at New York Comic Con when I occupy a table for a video call with Anthony Boyle. Beyond a bit part in Game of Thrones and roles in the movies Tolkien (2019) and Tetris (2023), Boyle’s growing body of work wouldn’t bring him to the East Coast’s nerd mecca. To wit: In 2024, he was on the FX series Say Nothing, with childhood friend Lola Petticrew, about the decades-long Troubles in Northern Ireland. Last year he starred in House of Guinness, a Netflix series about the famed brewery.

Sources indicate that soon he’ll appear in I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning, about tight-knit friends with unfulfilled dreams in the UK, which drew rave reviews at Cannes. After that, a mysterious project simply titled The Worst, “about all the worst people in the world,” Boyle teases. His costars include Keira Knightley and Alicia Vikander. There’s not a lightsaber or CGI monster in any of them.

According to recent reports, but you might call his latest role supervillain-worthy. On the Netflix series The Altruists, Boyle steps into the shoes of Sam Bankman-Fried. The crypto billionaire and founder of FTX, whose peak net worth was an estimated $26 billion, is now serving a 25-year sentence for fraud, conspiracy, and money laundering. Boyle plays Bankman-Fried at different times in his life, from his days on the bottom rungs of trading firms to his meteoric rise and catastrophic downfall. The series also explores his relationship with Caroline Ellison (Julia Garner), the Alameda Research CEO who was instrumental in FTX’s fraud.

Part business thriller and part romantic dramedy, The Altruists is like if The Social Network cornered Natural Born Killers at a bar to talk blockchain. For its leading man, that world was foreign. When FTX declared bankruptcy in November 2022 and Bankman-Fried was arrested a month later, Boyle’s attention was … not there. “I wasn’t following at all,” he tells me. “I’m not interested in crypto or finance.” But he knows a love story, even a doomed one, when he sees it. “I was more interested in Sam and Caroline’s relationship when the script was presented to me. Crypto was a backdrop. The show is about love and the complexity within that love. If you love someone, tell them. That’s the overriding message.”.

Unlike Boyle’s portrayal of Bankman-Fried—nervous, indirect, lacking steadfast confidence—the actor himself is warm and relaxed. His blunt eloquence and honesty are flavored with his Belfast accent. Even after playing a real-life (former) tech billionaire for an eight-hour miniseries, he remains disconnected from that archetype. “The only one I researched was Sam. But I don’t think we should have a system where people can become billionaires,” he indicates. “It feels wrong. There’s people starving on the streets of Manhattan, where we’re talking now, and there’s a billionaire in a high-rise. That seems to me a failed system.”.

Industry observers note that before streaming shows and acclaimed movies at Cannes, Boyle’s career came from especially humble beginnings. He used a wheelchair as a child, and he learned to improvise full conversations while watching other children play. While in high school, he was one of a handful of boys at an all-girls school and took on many of the male roles in the drama department.

Sources indicate that then he watched the 2006 movie This Is England. “Have you seen it?” Boyle asks me while anime characters pass by. I haven’t, though I vividly recall adding it to my Netflix queue once. “I thought it was the most incredible thing, like a lightning bolt, watching that movie. Thinking, I would love to do what they’re doing. It felt exhilarating and inspiring. It made an impression on me.”.

In a recent development, boyle and Lola Petticrew, who drew acclaim for their work in the Hulu series Furious, tried out for every audition they could find. “We would Google ‘Belfast acting auditions,’ ” Boyle notes. Once, they did a production of Romeo & Juliet that Boyle says was “awful.”.

“It was set on a chessboard, for some reason. I was dressed as David Bowie, during his Ziggy Stardust era, and Lola was Gene Simmons from Kiss. I could only move in an L-shape, like the knight. Lola could only move like a pawn, and they had to curtsy every time they moved.”.

Recent findings suggest that he laughs thinking about it now. “You look at moments like this, when you’re doing something that you actually love, you’re like, ‘It adds up.’ ”.

In an interview with Esquire, Anthony Boyle reveals how he got into the mind of someone like Sam Bankman-Fried, his formative experience on Game of Thrones, and what cosplay he might attempt if he could ever go to Comic Con.

This interview has been edited for clarity.

ESQUIRE: There are countless Sam Bankman-Fried interviews and documentaries about FTX. For The Altruists, how much did you let all this material inform your performance, and how much did you rely on your own instincts as an actor?

Recent findings suggest that ANTHONY BOYLE: You do a bit of both. You try to consume everything. Read all the books, watch every interview 5 million times. When you’re cycling or walking, you got headphones on, listening to his voice. It becomes part of your life—just trying to nail that voice. Trying to get into his head and mannerisms as much as possible. But on the first day of filming, I stopped. I stopped listening to his voice, stopped watching or reading anything [about him]. At day one, it became “our” Sam. Do as much research, fill your cup, then just forget about it.

After all that time listening and watching Sam, what were your impressions of him?

Recent findings suggest that I was bowled over by his intelligence. I think when you’re blessed with these things like “genius,” you’re also cursed. It’s hard to function. Look at great thinkers like Nikola Tesla. He was in love with a pigeon. When you’re [one of these] great minds, you’re often plagued with not being able to have relationships with people. Sam, in his own words, struggles. It was a joy to play someone who was so different to me and so complex.

How did you embody Sam’s nervous and manic energy?

Industry observers note that the nervousness is so key to him. In all the footage of him, you see his leg sort of going underneath the table. You listen to what he claims about himself in the therapy scenes: “I’m a failure, people are gonna find out I’m a failure.” Repeating that in your head before a scene and having your heart rate going, just trying to constantly quell a panic attack and just thinking the pressure cooker he’s in—I love this girl and I need to be a success—repeating these things, you start to get nervous and you use that nervous energy.

At the top of the series, Sam talks a lot about effective altruism. What was your understanding of that concept? Was Sam an effective effective altruist?

Being altruistic is being charitable. It is giving. To be altruistic, you could say, “I want to save lives.” Effective altruism would be “I go to Wall Street, make as much money as possible, and pay a hundred doctors to go save lives.” It’s trying to do the most good that you can do in the world. Did he succeed? In our version, he definitely tries to. He gets corrupted by power in our version of the story.

Recent findings suggest that so much of The Altruists is about this doomed love story with Caroline Ellison, played by Julia Garner. What was your experience working with her, playing out a volatile relationship?

Recent findings suggest that amazing. One of the best I’ve ever worked with, an incredible force of nature. It was an education to work. I honestly feel like, working with Julia every day, I picked up something. Some scenes, we’re just having fun. Whatever comes to mind, being playful and improvisational. And then there are scenes where we’re locked in, being so aggressive and nasty with one another. Those days felt good. It feels bad when you’re doing it. Your body doesn’t know you’re acting. It’s like, This is a good feeling because I know what’s happening is what I want. Working with her was like leveling up.

Is there a line of yours that best summarizes or reveals to us everything about Sam Bankman-Fried?

Industry observers note that when he speaks to Caroline and says, “I am FTX.” That is so integral to who he is. He built this huge empire. I was saying in an interview earlier, broken men build empires. He feels broken. If he is FTX, and FTX is the biggest, the best, the fastest, the greatest, then he is. If he built this thing, then that’s who he is, not this broken individual.

The Altruists positions itself as an unlikely love story set against financial fraud. But this was a real story where people lost their livelihoods. How can one reconcile the romantic-dramedy half of the show with the half where millions of real people are victims?

Industry observers note that there’s a dissonance, isn’t there? I understand. I think [the victims] would be right about how they feel. You can’t tell a victim of a crime how they should feel. Alex Lawther’s character reminds Sam that this isn’t just ones and zeroes. This is real people losing money. This isn’t just rich people playing. It’s heartbreaking. So many people committed suicide, got divorced, lost everything. That’s the through line with Alex Lawther’s character. He’s the voice of reason that reminds our audience there’s real life at stake.

Recent findings suggest that the Altruists is one of several newly introduced pieces of media about the tech industry and the billionaires behind them. There’s The Social Reckoning, Artificial, You Can See Everything. Why are we interested in these stories right now?

According to recent reports, it’s so interesting. I didn’t know any of these projects were happening until this morning, doing this press tour. These people are shaping our lives, and people are interested in how these sort of masked men behind closed doors are controlling everything. All we’re hearing in the news is AI recently, like AI is gonna kill us all. Makes us think of I, Robot or something. It’s interesting to get behind into these people’s brains and go, “What are they motivated by? What’s pushing them?”.

One of your earliest acting credits was for one episode of Game of Thrones, as a guard. What did that job mean for you as a very new actor at the time?

It was great. It was my first time on a proper set. I remember a fancy car picking me up, everyone in my street waving me off, shouting like, “Go on, off to Hollywood!” I was in the front seat, beeping the horn. The driver was like, “This has never happened.” I remember not knowing what was happening on set. I remember Gemma Whelan and Alfie Allen being so kind. I had two lines, and they were like, “Do you wanna run the lines? Do you wanna run them again?” They took care of me. I think of that every time I see someone young on set. Reach out to them, tell them they’re doing a good job. Give ’em a nod. It can be a scary environment when you’re not used to it.

Industry observers note that your very next thing is I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning. What is it about, and what does it mean to you?

In a recent development, it’s sort of about capitalism in the way The Altruists is. This is about family and friends in a community and how the working class in England and the Midlands have been decimated by the Tory government. It’s a socialist war cry by Keiran Goddard and Enda Walsh, one of the great Irish writers. He wrote Hunger and Disco Pigs. He remarked he had written this role with me in mind. It was a pinch-me moment, because I’d read his plays at school and would have given my left arm to work with him. When he sent me a letter, I was overjoyed.

Industry observers note that I also got a TV show that I’m excited about, Close to Home. It’s my first time executive producing. The guy who wrote it sat beside my brother in school. It’s about a guy who punches someone on a night out, gets arrested for it, and has to confront his life choices. It’s close to my heart because it’s about West Belfast, where I grew up.

In the spirit of Comic Con going on behind me, do you have a weird interest or fandom? If you were here, who would you be dressed as?

[Laughs.] Van Morrison. I would be dressed as Van Morrison. I’m obsessed with him. He is my favorite singer and an incredible musician. I listen to performances he’s done, like 1972 in Fresh York. I listen to deep cuts. I would be at Comic Con dressed up as him, which wouldn’t be a great costume. The winged angel might be better.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Abercrombie & Fitch’s resurgence has been well documented, and the brand highlights no signs of slowing down. Alongside its familiar mix of timeless staples, contemporary silhouettes, and archival-inspired pieces, Abercrombie has introduced YPB, or Your Personal Best: a dedicated line of performance apparel designed to bring the same considered approach to the gym as it does to the rest of your wardrobe.

Comprising everything from tees and tanks to shorts and jackets, YPB reflects Abercrombie’s ability to evolve while staying true to its heritage. The collection makes a convincing case for performance wear that goes beyond the usual sea of uninspired basics and head-to-toe Lycra. It’s also versatile enough to seamlessly move from a strenuous workout to the everyday wardrobe rotation. To put the collection through its paces, we’ve styled three looks that show just how far YPB can go.

It has been revealed that I am a chronic overheater so my gym outfits always reveal a bit of skin. (It’s also a vanity thing so I can see my muscles at work when I’m getting after it.) This vintage-inspired muscle tank looks like some of the actual vintage tees that I’ve taken a pair of scissors to without a stranger’s set-in stains. I have a lot of hair that gets in my way so headwear is a must when working out. A bandana is a nice throwback to the classic bodybuilder era and unlike a hat, it does a better job at soaking up the sweat so it’s not dripping down my face.

The standout of this outfit is the shorts. Compression lined, they’re about as long as I’d go for shorts clocking in with a five-inch inseam. They have a discreet pocket in the liner to store my phone, and they're tight enough so my device doesn’t go flying out when I’m doing high knees. Plus, they’re stretchy enough for hitting depth on a squat without risking a NSFW tear between the cheeks.

I’ve come to learn that recovery days are not only a blessing but a necessity. But they don’t necessarily mean you have to waste away on the couch all day. My active recovery days involve a lot of walking, and that means my workout shorts make an appearance once again. I can’t deny their comfort factor, and it’s hard to beat a sweater-and-shorts combo, an outfit beloved by my favorite A-listers.

Industry observers note that the sweater was a quarter-zip with an elastic waistband for a more streamlined, tailored fit. And if I’m walking a little too briskly, the top easily comes off to reveal a staple graphic tee in my wardrobe.

Finally, I put on some pants! I don’t make it a habit to wear sweatpants out casually, but sometimes the weather calls for it. Hike ‘em up a bit and show off some crisp white socks, a style swerve I saw once and couldn’t help but copy.

Industry observers note that the staple of this outfit is the heavyweight jacket. Its water-resistant lining keeps me dry when the meteorologists get the forecast wrong, and it’s lined to keep me warm as the days get shorter and the nights get longer. The two-way zipper also allows for some extra mobility, and it won’t bunch up when I sit down like so many other parkas.

Sources indicate that if you’re wondering what else there is to know about Cyrus and Morando’s low-key romance, then look no further. Below, we’ve tracked the couple’s entire relationship from start to finish.

For Cyrus, it was love at first sight, but for Morando, he already had an idea of who he was meeting long before the date even happened.

Their collaboration is the perfect example of sustainability becoming the next fashion phase, and it proves that anything can be reinvented, which resonates with me deeply.”.

The pair spark dating rumors when they make their first public appearance at the Gucci Love Parade fashion show in November.

A source tells People where Cyrus’s head is at amid her relationship with Morando.

(Even the player with the most modest initial following, Cyrus Irani, had over 10,000 followers at the time his casting was unveiled. Is it a problem? Not necessarily. But it’s certainly a switch-up from season 1’s social media skeptic Shubham Goel.).

The revival series is also airing in near-real time, with fresh episodes dropping Tuesday through Thursday and audience voting being used to shape the process. And perhaps the biggest change: stepping into hosting duties in place of comedian and actor Michelle Buteau is SiriusXM’s Christina “Tinx” Najjar, who rose to fame on social media during the COVID-19 pandemic.

It has been revealed that as a longtime Circle devotee, I was...curious about what these changes might mean for my favorite competition series. So when I got the chance to fly to Atlanta to visit the set (and meet Tinx) myself, I took it. There I chatted with her about the power of social media, the potential problem of having celebs in the Circle, and the player she thinks might win it all.

I truly couldn’t believe it. I know how many loyal fans The Circle has, so when I got the call that I got it—I mean, I’m still pinching myself every day. It’s a really big moment for me, and I know I have big shoes to fill. And I really just want to make everybody proud.

I remember watching the very first episode and thinking, “Wow, this is such a fresh concept, and it’s truly a social experiment for the modern age.” So the fact that I’m here all these years later is truly a pinch-me moment.

I relate to it so much, because in COVID, I was living in a studio apartment in L.A. I had just moved. I didn’t have a lot of friends, and all I had was my phone. That’s why I initially picked up TikTok and thought, “Who knows what’s going to happen in the world? I might as well make a few videos and try to make friends online.” And as soon as I started creating content, I just realized, “Wow, I love connecting with people. I love entertaining people.” It’s been a wild six years ever since.

It has been revealed that I grew up doing theater in high school, but honestly, no. I truthfully had a lot of limiting beliefs about myself. I just thought there was no way I could ever be an influencer. I didn’t feel pretty enough. I didn’t think I was put together enough. And I think one thing COVID taught us is that anybody who has a dream can go for it. Social media is really the great equalizer in that sense, because if you are funny, if you have something to say, you can get online and you can connect with people.

It has been revealed that it’s such an honor, and I love that people look up to me for advice. It’s the honor of my life that people trust me enough to call me on my radio show for advice or write to me, and I just try to be a voice of reason and remind women to know their worth. I feel like this is a journey I was meant to be on, and all of the opportunities that being online has afforded me, because it really has given me so much. The fact that I’m sitting here as the host of The Circle is—again, I can’t believe it.

It’s so different because I’m used to just holding up my phone, recording, cutting swiftly, and pressing post. This is a totally different operation, but the crew is so cool, production is so cool, and the writers that I work with are just so smart and so funny. I was actually shocked when they explained to me the process of how close to the wire we are. It is as close to real time as you could ever think.

In a recent development, because I have lived online for six years, I post in real time myself. I’m someone who wakes up and I’m like, “Hey guys, I’m going to the gym. Here’s what I’m eating for breakfast.” I don’t know if I would know how to do it any other way, because I’m just, like, an oversharer, so I think I would just be myself and see what happened. But I can be strategic. I feel like I would make a lot of alliances. I’m good at that.

I honestly think maybe the celebrities are at a slight disadvantage because, as you say, people have perceptions about them. I feel like they also have more of a target on their backs.

It has been revealed that he was shocked. He had such a good strategy. I was honestly shocked he got out, too. He’s so likable, and everyone knew it was really him. He got got. He got got by Justin [Hinsley], if I’m being honest, who has very strong strategy. I think Justin is incredibly strategic and knows how to play the game.

According to recent reports, I think it’s totally fine, because there’s a lot on the line here. This is a popularity contest, but there’s a big prize at the end. So I think it’s fun when people are ruthless. Why not? It’s a game, and games are meant to be won.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., leaves a meeting in the Capitol on Tuesday, before his election as incoming minority leader later in the day.
  • Senate Majority Leader John Thune was reelected as the Republican leader on Tuesday and will steer the conference through their time in the minority.
  • The South Dakotan ran uncontested despite a push from some of his colleagues to delay the leadership elections following Republicans’ stunning defeats last week in the midterms, which saw them lose at least seven seats and the majority.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., leaves a meeting in the Capitol on Tuesday, before his election as incoming minority leader later in the day. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Majority Leader John Thune was reelected as the Republican leader on Tuesday and will steer the conference through their time in the minority.

The South Dakotan ran uncontested despite a push from some of his colleagues to delay the leadership elections following Republicans’ stunning defeats last week in the midterms, which saw them lose at least seven seats and the majority.

According to recent reports, “Obviously, the election result was not what we hoped for,” Thune told reporters, referring to the midterms. “But I think it’s vital that we take the lessons from that and internalize the message the American people were sending to us.”.

While he and the rest of the leadership slate sailed through the conference contests by voice vote, it wasn’t without drama.

Recent findings suggest that before the leadership elections began in the Old Supreme Court Chamber early Tuesday morning, the conference held a meeting at the request of a group of GOP five senators, led by Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis.

In a recent development, the conversation, which several senators described as “frank,” ended up pushing back the leadership elections by a few hours. But they were not postponed to another day as some had hoped.

In a recent development, “This has never been anything against John Thune,” remarked Johnson, as he made good on his commitment to leave the room early if the conference proceeded with its election. “What I didn’t agree with was holding the election right away, giving nobody an opportunity to really challenge any leadership position.”.

“Part of the concern here is who wants the job? God bless him for serving,” Johnson added.

The conference conversation Tuesday morning turned into an “open-mic” with both conservatives and those who lost their elections speaking, according to senators.

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., told reporters, “To rush into this and to just ratify all the same leadership — I mean, what message does that send?”.

Sources indicate that but no contender to Thune emerged despite the angst, and a motion to proceed to the election, introduced by Thune’s fellow South Dakotan Sen. Mike Rounds, was accepted.

According to recent reports, sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., stated voters who rejected Republicans last week were reacting to high gas prices, the war in Iran and the cost of living, not to how Senate leaders were running the conference.

“I don’t think anybody in Texas who voted for the Democrat governor was voting against John Thune. If you diagnose that as a problem, you’re misdiagnosing the problem,” Paul stated.

Recent findings suggest that whip John Barrasso, R-Wyo., was reelected to his position, as was the chairman of the Senate Republican Conference, Tom Cotton of Arkansas. Sen. James Lankford of Oklahoma was again selected as vice chair of the conference, while Sen. Shelley Moore Capito of West Virginia was reelected as Republican Policy Committee chair.

It has been revealed that “Our first step is to make sure the American people know that we heard what they said, and the American people’s priorities are our priorities. That’s the way we regain their trust,” Barrasso said afterward.

Recent findings suggest that sen. Bernie Moreno of Ohio got the nod to chair the National Republican Senatorial Committee, meaning he will helm the campaign arm as the party looks ahead to the uncertain waters of 2028.

Moreno stated, “I was in the retail automobile business, so when you don’t listen to your customers, your customers punish you. I think we have to own it, and I think we have to learn from it.”.

Sources indicate that sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said on Monday evening, “What we as a conference right now need is honesty. We need focus. We need to try to reach a consensus on what we need to change.”.

Kennedy was among those pushing to delay the leadership elections and told reporters on Tuesday he voted present instead of yes on whether to proceed to them.

Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., who ran for GOP leader twice — once in 2022 against Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., and in 2024 against Thune — declined to run again to challenge Thune. But in a Dear Colleague letter on Monday, he detailed what he’d like to see in the lame-duck session before Democrats take power, including confirming every nominee President Donald Trump has sent to the Senate, funding the government without an omnibus, banning stock trading, passing the permitting bill that is advancing this week in the Senate, passing the National Defense Authorization Act, balancing the budget and pushing through a sweeping voter ID bill known as the SAVE America Act.

Senate Republicans on Tuesday also voted on a resolution on their path forward that was spurred by a motion from Scott, aides mentioned.

Sources indicate that “It is the sense of the GOP Conference that we will maximize the 54 days we have with congressional majorities, to confirm every judicial nominee and every executive nominee that the conference approves of, to pass our core Republican priorities, and to do everything humanly possible to pass a reconciliation bill before Jan. 3,” the resolution reads in part.

Recent findings suggest that that long list of goals highlights the expectations Thune has faced as leader, where he led one-third of Republicans’ trifecta in Washington. In the next Congress, Democrats will hold the majority in both chambers of Congress after their larger-than-expected wins, while Trump finishes out his term as president.

Thune stated he told his conference: “As I look back on the last couple of years, my question is, what would you have me do differently?”.

“Given the constraints we had to deal with, all the stuff that was coming at us on a daily basis, a narrow margin in the House, the White House, the Democrats over here who were obstructing two long government shutdowns — I think we came out of it as well as could have been expected, and got a lot of stuff done,” Thune told reporters.

Industry observers note that “If you believe the exit polls, it was the war, it was the economy, it was inflation, it was fuel prices,” Thune added. “So no, I wasn’t apologizing for anything that we did. And I think on the political side, I don’t know what else I could have done.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, if you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

According to recent reports, whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

Sources indicate that toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

It has been revealed that heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

Add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

Sources indicate that add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that gordon Ramsay has earned 17 Michelin stars throughout his career and still oversees nearly 100 restaurants. He also fronts prime-time TV franchises on both sides of the Atlantic and holds a couple of casual Guinness World Records (call him if you need to fillet a 10-pound fish in 1 minute five seconds).

In a recent development, this is a man who’s never met a goalpost he didn’t want to surpass. So it wasn’t entirely surprising when he posted a bare-chested shot of his six-pack to the grid earlier this month. What generated headlines was the occasion: his 60th birthday. “Gordon Ramsay thirst trap was not on my bingo card,” reads one comment. “My wife is on this app sir,” reads another.

Industry observers note that at home in London, he demonstrates me the Insights section on his Instagram account, which reveals the photo has gotten over 62 million impressions. “It’s very strange,” he states. “I’ve had a lot of ribbing from my eldest daughter, Megan. She’s a police officer. She was like, ‘Dad, how can you do that to me?’ All her senior sergeants and officers were laughing and telling her to tell me they’re going for a run. They’re in their early 40s. And then my Royal Marines Commando son just sent me a message with: ‘WTF dad, what are you doing?’”.

According to recent reports, ramsay has been a pretty active guy for a while now, despite working in an industry typically associated with chaotic diets and zero time for exercise. He was a youth soccer player back in the day, before becoming a chef and then, in his 40s, going from weighing 252 pounds to competing in marathons and Ironmans.

All very impressive, but it’s even rarer to be this chiseled in your 60s (maintaining a low body fat percentage becomes harder as your testosterone and growth hormone production slows down). Read on to learn more about his preferred forms of cardio, his favorite pre-workout treat, and why he's established a daily cryotherapy routine. “I call it my freezer,” he indicates.

“15 minutes a day. It starts off with a quick two-minute stretch and 100 sit-ups every morning. Precore lifestyle is my ab cruncher thing—these things are fucking amazing, by the way. If I miss a day, then I have to punish it and do double the next day.”.

Sources indicate that “It’s not physically hard with massive weights. These are 25 pounds. I’ll do a strength class once a week, 45 minutes. That’s it. Occasional push-ups and squats. No personal trainer.”.

“What’s helped tremendously, with no impact on any of the joints, is a lot of swimming. So I have an injury in my patella, my right knee, currently. So I just increased the swimming because that’s the only sport that can use every muscle in your body with zero impact. But cardio is off the charts.”.

It has been revealed that “I have a Zwift bike, so I jump on that for 45 minutes. There’s no impact on that. I’ll do that Monday, Wednesday, Friday and gear up for 90 minutes on a Sunday. If I wasn’t injured, I’d be doing three 5K runs again, Monday, Wednesday, Friday, 20-minute runs. I’ve got my 5K back down to 21 minutes. The dream is under 20. I was running at 19 and a half back in July. A 5K run is easy to do in the morning before work, it’s done within half an hour. Once I do that, I can gear up for either a two-hour bike on a Sunday or a 90-minute run. I alternate. So, one Sunday’s run, one Sunday’s bike.”.

Recent findings suggest that “10 years ago, I ruptured my Achilles. I invested in an AlterG, a beautiful running machine that takes your weight, so you get all the cardio you want and less impact on the joint.”.

“From the chef’s perspective, I call it my freezer. It’s the cryochamber. I do two sets of three minutes every morning. I try to go seven days a week in that thing, straight after [working out]. That is incredible. That’ll get up to like minus 160. For six minutes.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I’ve invested in a tiny little red-light therapy sauna outside in the garden, and it seats two of you, and so [I’ll do] half an hour of that, every other day. This doesn’t need to be done every day. Three times a week’s fine. So when I’m not running, the other day I’ll sit in that red-light therapy and spend 20 minutes, 30 minutes in there, which is brilliant.”.

“The older you get, the more you have to stretch. I use a lot of bands. And so after sitting and stretching, I had those incredible bands where you lift your feet up and pull and stretch. 5 minutes is always a nice stretch before you [work out] and then 10 minutes stretch after that. I’ve never been to a yoga class in my life.”.

According to recent reports, “I’m major on oatmeal for breakfast, Monday to Friday. I indulge Saturday, Sunday. I will do [oatmeal with] blueberry compote, caramelized banana for my potassium, and then fresh blueberries on top with some—it sounds weird, but it’s delicious—hot honey.”.

“I have my friends at Precision. I’ll do one of their gels before I start that 5K, a protein gel, 30 grams, and then that sees me through the whole 45-minute routine. Coffee is just a full-fat, flat white, extra hot. Extra hot means I can sip it slowly. I cut out a lot of dairy, a lot of butter, a lot of cream. And so that treat in the morning with a flat white is that sort of, ‘I’ve earned this shit.’”.

“I don’t overstress on that because I stay fit. I monitor what I eat, but if anything, I’ll do smaller portions now. I’ll involve a lot of spinach, involve a lot of salmon, chicken, especially thighs. We’re just smart with less cream, less butter intake. And then when we travel, we just keep it light.”.

“I have a red wine with dinner, Californian, something light, something delicious. In 20, 30 years running restaurants, I’ve never gone around the room holding a glass of wine, holding a glass of champagne, sitting down, drinking with customers. Again, discipline.”.

“Just a couple of spoons of creatine, five mornings a week. A little scoop in my water.”.

It has been revealed that “One thing I’ve learned in my 50s and my 60s—everyone said the older you get, the less you sleep. I think it’s the other way around. I like to be in bed by 11, and I’m up at 6. My Oura ring for me has become my best mate, because it just gives me the proper day-by-day indication and then keeps you on track for sleep.”.

Sources indicate that “No, no, no, no, no, no. Definitely not. No. I mean, no. My meditation is Kitchen fucking Nightmares. Dealing with some of those contributors on there and having to sit with them and talk with them. But no, not very good at sitting still.”.

#169124. Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing

Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1050 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • FCC nominee Danielle Thumann Severs waits to testify during her confirmation hearing with the Senate Commerce Committee on Tuesday.
  • President Donald Trump's Republican nominee to the Federal Communications Commission faced opposition Tuesday from Senate Democrats who fear the commission could be controlled exclusively by Republicans under Chairman Brendan Carr, who they vowed to investigate in the next Congress.
  • Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee, nominee Danielle Thumann Severs limited her commitments to independence from Carr, including on regulating broadcasters based on their content decisions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

FCC nominee Danielle Thumann Severs waits to testify during her confirmation hearing with the Senate Commerce Committee on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

President Donald Trump's Republican nominee to the Federal Communications Commission faced opposition Tuesday from Senate Democrats who fear the commission could be controlled exclusively by Republicans under Chairman Brendan Carr, who they vowed to investigate in the next Congress.

Appearing before the Senate Commerce Committee, nominee Danielle Thumann Severs limited her commitments to independence from Carr, including on regulating broadcasters based on their content decisions.

Much of the hearing focused on Carr and his threats to use the FCC to punish broadcasters he disagrees with.

Industry observers note that sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., said that he expects Carr will not last long in his position once Democrats take control of Congress in the latest year.

“Mr. Carr, if you're listening now, know you're going to be in this body once a month, if not more, and in the House of Representatives as well, answering questions … so we can get to the bottom of the nonsense and the cover-ups that have been taking place,” Luján mentioned.

The nomination of Thumann Severs, who right now serves as senior counsel to Carr, has led to consternation among Democrats due to continued vacancies at the FCC. The five-member commission is intended to have three members of the president’s party, including the chair, and two in the minority.

According to recent reports, currently Carr serves alongside fellow Republican Olivia Trusty and Democrat Anna M. Gomez, whose term expired earlier this year. Gomez may continue to serve through next year under the law if a replacement is not nominated and confirmed.

Democrats are concerned that if Thumann Severs were to be confirmed, the commission’s three Republican members could constitute a quorum on their own, allowing Trump to fire Gomez.

Sen. John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., mentioned Senate precedent is to move pairs of one Democratic and one Republican nominee for the FCC and that he “strongly” believed the Thumann Severs nomination should have been paired with a renomination of Gomez in order to continue having “both parties at the table.”.

“A bipartisan FCC is essential to avoid things like large-scale media consolidation [and] I think also, more fundamentally, to protect a free and diverse press [that] serves everyone,” Hickenlooper said.

In addition to urging Trump to renominate Gomez, Democrats underlined the need for a second Democratic member of the commission.

Hickenlooper highlighted Thumann Severs’ close work with Carr, who Democrats and some Republicans have been critical of for comments about using the FCC’s public interest standard against television stations airing programming Carr disagrees with.

Thumann Severs’ work at the FCC right now focuses on the Wireline, Public Safety and Homeland Security, and Consumer and Governmental Affairs bureaus, rather than the Media Bureau.

Committee Chair Ted Cruz, R-Texas, has also been critical of Carr’s comments. On Tuesday, he listed the FCC’s request for ABC-owned stations to submit early license renewals alongside earlier incidents in which he remarked Democrats encouraged the weaponization of the FCC against conservative voices.

Industry observers note that “The First Amendment places important limits on the government’s ability to regulate speech,” Cruz stated. “The FCC possesses significant regulatory authority over communications, so there is always a risk that it could weaponize its authority against Americans with whom it disagrees.”.

Thumann Severs committed to Cruz that she would base licensing decisions on “the law and the record” and not use the FCC’s authority to “pressure or punish” broadcasters for protected speech.

It has been revealed that however, when Sen. Edward J. Markey, D-Mass., questioned Thumann Severs on whether the FCC could punish broadcasters the president disagreed with, Thumann Severs repeated one of Carr’s arguments in discussing the FCC’s role.

Industry observers note that “Broadcasters are subject to public interest obligations as part of the public trustee model in exchange for the licenses that they hold,” she remarked. “As part of those public interest obligations, they are subject to many different rules and requirements, and the FCC is charged with enforcing and investigating the public interest standard against broadcasters.”.

Under repeated questions from Markey about Carr’s previous remarks, Thumann Severs said she would base her decisions “in the facts and the law and the record.”.

Sources indicate that luján also asked Thumann Severs to name problems where she had disagreed with Carr or Trump. While she mentioned her decisions would be her own, she declined to name any examples of disagreement.

In addition to questions about Carr, Democrats asked the nominee about the FCC’s E-Rate program, which provides low-cost connectivity for schools and libraries, and the Universal Service Fund, which funds the E-Rate program and other programs.

Thumann Severs said that she believes the E-Rate program has been successful and that the FCC has a statutory obligation to provide some kind of discounted service to schools and libraries. But she was less forthcoming on whether the FCC could shut down the program as it at the moment exists without congressional approval or whether the program should be restricted only to rural areas.

Late last month, Democratic members of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, led by Communications and Technology Subcommittee ranking member Doris Matsui, D-Calif., sent a letter to Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and Cruz urging Gomez’s renomination with any move to confirm a Republican nominee.

Sources indicate that “Commissioner Gomez has shown the experience and judgment to continue that work,” the members wrote. “We therefore ask that the Senate pair any upcoming Republican nominee with her renomination to a full term, consistent with the bipartisan design Congress built into this agency.”.

On Monday, the Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights also sent a letter to committee leadership urging a delay on the hearing and any vote on Thumann Severs’ nomination until Gomez can be renominated.

“Independent agencies should not be extensions of presidential will: their leaders should exercise independent judgement based on their expertise and statutory mandates,” the group wrote.

Cruz did not indicate Tuesday when the committee might vote on Thumann Severs’ nomination, and no markup has yet been announced by the committee of hers' and those of three others for two posts at NASA and one at the Transportation Department who also testified.

#169118. A Brief Guide to Grand Theft Auto VI’s Nike Sneaker Dupes

A Brief Guide to Grand Theft Auto VI’s Nike Sneaker Dupes

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that GTA 6 is finally out, which means we’ve got some in-game sneaker shopping to do.
  • Nike takes its name from the Greek goddess of victory, while Eris is the goddess of strife and discord—an appropriate choice for kicks you might buy with money from an armed robbery.
  • The Eris Rise Low is the obvious starting point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that GTA 6 is finally out, which means we’ve got some in-game sneaker shopping to do. We’d already spotted Air Force 1 dupes in the trailers, but now that we can finally play the long-awaited masterpiece itself, we’re taking a closer look at what else is on the shelves. There are tons of different sneaker stores sprinkled throughout the game, and Eris—Rockstar’s fictional answer to Nike—has given us a lot to work through.

Even the name is a joke. Nike takes its name from the Greek goddess of victory, while Eris is the goddess of strife and discord—an appropriate choice for kicks you might buy with money from an armed robbery. The Swoosh has been replaced with a pointier, upside-down logo, and plenty of the sneakers baring the mark are instantly recognizable.

The Eris Rise Low is the obvious starting point. It’s the game’s AF1 equivalent, complete with the familiar paneled upper, perforated toebox, and a massive, beefy sole underfoot. The Eris Strife 360, meanwhile, looks straight out of the Air Max 97 catalog. There’s the rippling upper, rounded toe, and long cushioning window underneath. Designed by Christian Tresser and released in 1997, the IRL sneaker’s silhouette took inspiration from water ripples, while the OG “Silver Bullet” finish drew on mountain bike components. Eris keeps enough of that shape for you to be able to spot it from across the shop.

Off-White x Nike Air Max 97 ‘White’.

Recent findings suggest that some versions get even more specific. There’s a white-and-orange Strife 360, for example, with oversized branding, contrasting lace loops, and printed side text that recalls Off-White’s own Air Max 97s. It isn’t a straight one-to-one recreation, but the reference feels pretty clear. An apparent take on the Off-White Air Force 1 Mid also appeared in the teasers. Someone at Rockstar is clearly a fan of Virgil Abloh’s work.

Then there’s the Eris Strife 90, with pairs that borrow heavily from the Air Max 90 “Infrared.” The bright red accents and sharp, aggressive lines are all there, with one colorway even adding black scribbles across the overlays.

Arguably the most iconic signature shoe of all time, the Air Jordan 1, gets a look in the game as well. The Eris Rook 1 High comes in leather and suede variations, with a tall ankle collar and laces running almost all the way up. There’s a black-and-white pair that swaps Jordan branding for an Eris basketball graphic on the tongue. You’ve probably got something quite similar in your closet at home.

Air Jordan 1 High OG ‘Yin Yang’.

In a recent development, the Eris Cross Trainers are, well, harder to pin down. Available in several colorways, they have a mesh base and leather overlays. One white-and-gray version gets bright green hits that nod to Nike’s signature “Volt” hue. The simpler construction puts it closer to an older Nike runner, somewhere around MD Runner 2 territory, than a direct Zoom Vomero 5 or V5 Rnr copy. And for those times that tying laces feels like too much work, there are the very appropriately named Eris Basic Slides. The broad branded strap and flat footbed are very Nike Benassi.

There are different versions to consider, too. “Origins” go all-white, while “Elite” options are matte and all-black. So if you‘ve found a silhouette you like, you can still spend another 10 minutes deciding which version works with your trousers. A problem we were hoping to leave outside the game.

Industry observers note that it gives you an idea of just how much there is in GTA 6. The older games let you change your clothes, but here you’re choosing between different colorways, materials, and versions of individual shoes. And Eris is only one part of it: There are clothes and accessories that look like takes on Stüssy, Loewe, Chrome Hearts, and Louis Vuitton, too. You could spend a fair bit of time getting dressed before you get anything else done.

We’ve waited this long to play the game. A few more minutes in the sneaker shop before you really get going on missions won’t hurt.

A version of the story originally appeared on British GQ.

Steak Bites With Spinach Couscous

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (533 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare.
  • More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.
  • boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare. But cut a steak into bite-size pieces and suddenly it transforms into a quick-cooking protein that’s no more demanding than chicken breast or tofu. Rub the steak with the spices and make the quick no-recipe yogurt sauce a few hours ahead if it’s helpful with time management. To account for the extra liquid thrown off by the spinach as it cooks, the water-to-couscous ratio in this recipe differs from that often found on the back of the bag (or box) so measure accordingly.

More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.

Place 1–1¼ lb. boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp. dried oregano, 2 tsp. onion powder, 2 tsp. sugar, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl; season generously with freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. Let sit at least 10 minutes or cover and chill up to 8 hours (no need to bring to room temperature before cooking if chilling).

According to recent reports, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid over medium. Add 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced, ½ cup finely chopped dill, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until scallions are softened, about 5 minutes. Add 10 oz. baby spinach in 2–3 handfuls, stirring and letting wilt slightly after each addition before adding more, 5–7 minutes total. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil; season with more salt if needed. Add 1 cup Moroccan couscous and stir to break up any lumps. Remove from heat; quickly cover with lid and let sit 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over high. Arrange steak in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 6–8 minutes. Reduce heat to medium; continue to cook, stirring often, until meat is just cooked through, about 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Add remaining 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; toss to combine. (Residual heat from pan will cook out any raw garlic flavor.).

It has been revealed that uncover couscous and fluff with a fork to separate grains. Spoon into a large shallow bowl or onto a platter. Top with steak. Cut 1 lemon into quarters and squeeze juice from 1 quarter over steak. Scatter thinly sliced cucumber and some dill sprigs on top; drizzle with oil.

According to recent reports, combine 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt and a generous pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl; squeeze juice from 2 lemon quarters into yogurt. Stir to combine. If sauce is thick, stir in water, a spoonful at a time, to loosen.

Serve steak and couscous with yogurt sauce and remaining lemon quarter and more lemon wedges for squeezing over.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin hold a news conference calling for a “bold direction” for Senate Democrats on Tuesday.
  • Industry observers note that more Democrats emerged Tuesday wanting someone besides Senate Democratic leader Charles E.
  • Industry observers note that but Schumer maintained confidence he would be reelected to the post despite Sens.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sens. Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin hold a news conference calling for a “bold direction” for Senate Democrats on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

Industry observers note that more Democrats emerged Tuesday wanting someone besides Senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., to lead their conference in the majority.

Industry observers note that but Schumer maintained confidence he would be reelected to the post despite Sens. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., publicly calling for a different leader or a “concrete plan” that provides change.

“I’m confident I will be elected majority leader, and our caucus is really united in focusing on bringing down costs, on ending the corruption, on ending the chaos, on ending the war,” Schumer told reporters Tuesday. “We have great unity in our caucus, and I’ll be proud to lead it.”.

Sanders mentioned during a news conference Tuesday the election was about “change and the need for the Democratic Party to move in a new and bold direction.”.

According to recent reports, “I personally have known Chuck Schumer for over 30 years, and I like Chuck. Nobody works harder than Chuck Schumer. But in my view the time is now for change, and I will not be supporting Chuck to be reelected as the Democratic leader,” Sanders mentioned, calling for an “economy that works for all, not just the people on top.”.

“Do I think Chuck has been leading in that direction?” he asked. “No.”.

In a recent development, some incoming members and now incumbents have pointed to Maryland Democrat Chris Van Hollen as one possibility to challenge Schumer. Van Hollen had previously thrown cold water on the idea by saying he was instead “kicking the tires” on a presidential run in 2028 but has recently changed his tune.

A person familiar with Van Hollen’s thinking said he “has received an outpouring of calls on running for majority leader and is now in active listening mode.”.

Slotkin did not endorse anyone for leader but said she had a “really productive conversation” with Van Hollen yesterday.

“Whoever wants my vote is going to have to show me a concrete plan that’s definitely different. I’m a ‘no’ until and unless I see that from anyone,” she said, urging her peers to “withhold quorum” when Senate Democrats hold their leadership elections “until you get that plan and you feel like you have a voice in that plan.”.

She urged not just a roadmap for the first 100 days, but ideas for how to “communicate differently.” As for her own future, she said, “I am not actively seeking this job. I’m seeking change.”.

Asked about his looks Monday evening, Van Hollen said, “It’s not about me, but I am listening to the thousands of people who have been calling for change, but especially listening to our members, with a particular ear to fresh members who have just come off the campaign trail.”.

In a recent development, “What I’ve said from the very beginning is, we shouldn’t have a coronation. We should have a caucus discussion about what we're going to do with the power and responsibilities that have been invested in us,” Van Hollen said. “I’m in listening mode and haven’t shut the door.”.

According to recent reports, van Hollen took it a step further at an event Tuesday in Washington, D.C., criticizing the minority leader and Democrats’ campaign arm over their preferences in some primaries. “Schumer and the DSCC sided with the crypto industry and AIPAC against these candidates,” he mentioned, according to a livestream of the event.

In a recent development, schumer tried to tamp down the suggestion of a rivalry. “We talk frequently, and we’re united — united in lowering costs, and united in ending this damn war,” he said of Van Hollen.

Others threw their support behind Schumer ahead of the Democratic leadership elections, which are expected to take place in December.

Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee Chair Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y., praised Schumer for raising money and recruiting candidates like Sens.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio and Roy Cooper of North Carolina to help land at minimum seven seats, and potentially nine if Alaska and Mississippi ultimately swing their way.

It has been revealed that “That takes vision. It takes clarity of thought. It takes strategic leadership, and that is what Sen. Schumer has done. And that is why you will see, despite all grumblings, enormous gratitude,” she said.

Industry observers note that gillibrand pointed to candidates like Scott Colom, the Democrat in Mississippi who is currently leading GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a nail-biter of a race. “That wave doesn’t get created by magic. It gets created by hard work and putting the pieces together over years,” she stated.

Colom, however, has been noncommittal, telling MS NOW, “Too many of our leaders are from the same areas of the country,” pointing to the Brooklyn roots of both Schumer and current House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to run for speaker on the House side.

Sen. Ruben Gallego, D-Ariz., remarked he and Schumer have had their differences. But he implied he backs him for majority leader: “At the end of the day, these are historic numbers. It’s time for us to unify. We are going to work together as a caucus to blueprint together about how to move forward for what the country wants us to do, and I think we have the person who I think is going to lead us there.”.

Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., said Democrats have “an opportunity to do things differently, and I think we will, regardless of who the leader is. It doesn’t really matter whose name is on the door.”.

“Yes,” he stated of his support for Schumer, noting that so far, nobody has officially stepped up to the plate. “This is a guy that worked incredibly hard over the last couple of years. I know people have other opinions about this. But we have a mandate to do things and get things done for the American people.”.

“And we can do that with Chuck Schumer.”.

Sources indicate that mark Schoeff Jr., Paul M. Krawzak and Kelly Livingston contributed to this report.

#169109. Breaking: As an Awkward Teen, Grand Theft Auto Was My Escape. Now It Feels Like Real Life.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1693 w)
